Otherwise the driver reacquires the full requested scope and interval for that station and internal product route, with fetch padding; it does not request only uncovered dates. Other covered routes can still be reused. Successful interval replacements affect only their concrete series, physical facts and established intervals. A successful empty answer replaces the corresponding held rows too. Failed or unsupported acquisitions preserve held rows and successful coverage at their original retrieval instants; their outcomes and issues can still be recorded. Inventory evidence remains separate from successful coverage. Matching facts never allow one source identity to cover another.

A failure naming physical facts affects only those facts within its established window. An unspecified fact scope remains conservative within the concrete series or failed route. Inventory-only uncertainty does not invalidate independently successful observations. For example, a failed maximum-stage request preserves its held observations while a successful mean-stage request replaces its own observations, including a successful empty answer. Each fact keeps the acquisition time and calls that support it, including an unknown acquisition time. Independent facts do not share attribution merely because one transaction writes them together.

Explicit complete acquired fact membership can remain valid when a named member's observations fail. This membership evidence does not supply missing observation coverage. Retiring an older fact requires applicable complete acquired membership that establishes its absence, with valid inventory dependencies. Caller selection and missing rows do not authorize retirement; failed and unestablished fact scopes remain protected.

Both store kinds use the shared publication lifecycle described below. Partition files MUST NOT be modified in place. An accumulated update groups replacements by partition and rewrites each affected partition once. Unchanged partitions retain their original content identities through hardlinks. Metadata-only updates do not copy or decode observation partitions.

Current evidence is separate from a permanent attempt history. Coverage and retained observation keys identify the successful outcomes supporting saved data. A successful replacement supersedes earlier diagnostics only within its established identity, physical-fact and time-axis scope. Partial recovery leaves unresolved failures active. Fully superseded records can be removed only after their current data, coverage and inventory dependencies have been resolved. The internal supporting_outcomes relation keeps an original acquisition outcome only while a retained inventory still cites it. It is separate from active outcomes and MUST NOT contribute an active diagnostic or trigger caller issue policy. Compaction removes that support once its last current dependency is gone. Both relations require unique, consistent identities and valid source-call links. Reuse MUST NOT reactivate a superseded failure. Generated excerpts remain distinct from original publisher payloads.

Publisher payload bytes are not stored. A held receipt is a store excerpt encoded from selected physical rows, with served coverage and retrieval instants in provenance.

docs.title: Publication integrity and inspection
docs.text:
A published generation contains integrity.json alongside its manifest and partitions. An interrupted witness refresh can leave the reserved .integrity.pending metadata file. Inspection reports it as cleanup residue; normal reads and audit refuse it until explicit recovery checks the committed seal and removes that temporary file. It is never treated as published data. This seal records a closed inventory of managed files and their SHA-256 content identities. The generation identity binds the content inventory, including manifest.json. The seal also retains filesystem witnesses used only to detect whether unchanged partitions need another byte check during an update.

Publication MUST validate all new or changed observations, all metadata relations and the complete file inventory. Reused partitions MUST retain their previously validated content digests. Their identities, physical facts and acquisition support MUST remain valid under the new metadata. Bulk certification additionally checks complete source-column closure, source inventory/count/identity and exact source-to-staged-store equality. Local auditing does not repeat that source check.

Operations have distinct detection scopes:

Operation Checks performed cache_status Journal and ownership, closed file inventory, file identities, manifest digest and metadata relations. When recorded device, inode, size and modification-time witnesses match, no observation or annotation bytes are decoded or hashed; when they differ on an idle committed store, complete digest and observation validation runs once before updating local witnesses. Store read Current metadata and closed inventory, then original content digests for selected product/year observation and annotation partitions. When recorded witnesses differ on first access after copying, the complete store is validated and re-witnessed before reading. Published validation establishes observation consistency; verified bytes preserve that authority. Observation decoding applies conservative request predicates. audit_cache Every sealed file digest (including annotation partitions) and all observation and metadata consistency rules for one generation. Updates local witnesses if a complete copied store was not yet re-witnessed. Return identifies the generation and checked counts. Accumulated update Current metadata, new or changed observation and annotation partitions, and the retained support for unchanged partitions. Original digests are carried forward, never inferred from replacement bytes.

The selected-read boundary uses inspect_integrity and the shared selected-file hash checks. A public request shares metadata preparation and verified partition identities across its stations and routes. Before reusing preparation, the reader checks the closed inventory and filesystem witnesses, including change times. An owned publication invalidates this preparation. An unexpected generation change refuses the read rather than combining old metadata with new observations.

Metadata and inventory checks depend on the store size. Selected-file hashing reads each candidate partition in full. Parquet decoding applies station, time, source-series and physical-fact restrictions within those partitions; unrelated row groups can be skipped. A candidate row group can contain unrequested rows. This is bounded decoding, not a promise of one-row physical I/O. The conversion stage retains authority for physical conversion and exact clipping.

A small read need not discover changed observation bytes in an unselected partition when its structural file identities still agree. A relevant later read or audit_cache detects those changes. Missing files, extra files, incompatible metadata and unresolved lifecycle work still refuse access. Each new public request inspects current metadata; there is no permanent path-only trust.

A filesystem witness contains device, inode, size, modification time and change time. Owned hardlink creation and removal change the last field without changing content. Under exclusive ownership, the writer can record those known transitions while preserving the original digest. When device, inode, size or modification-time witnesses differ on a complete idle store, such as after copying a cache to another directory or machine, inspection verifies the closed file inventory, every file's saved size and SHA-256 digest, and all metadata and observation rules under the exclusive lease before atomically recording the new local witnesses in integrity.json. Subsequent operations use the normal witness check. Unfinished transaction paths, non-idle ownership, or .integrity.pending are not treated as relocated snapshots. Interrupted cleanup or witness replacement can require extra byte checks on recovery or the next update. Neither transition may cause changed bytes to acquire a new certified identity automatically.

Digests detect local corruption and ordinary replacement. They do not authenticate an attacker who can replace data and rewrite its seal. Concurrent external mutation and hostile local users are outside this contract.

docs.title: Shared publication and recovery
docs.text:
One shared transaction protocol covers compiled replacement and live accumulation. Their data replacement semantics remain distinct. A compiled snapshot replaces the previous snapshot, including legitimate removals. A live update replaces only established successful scopes.

An exclusive local-process lease coordinates download, compilation, accumulation, recovery and clear. The permanent .store.owner coordination file MUST NOT be unlinked while it can be opened by another process. The kernel releases ownership on process termination. Well-formed local abandoned ownership can be recovered; active or ambiguous ownership MUST refuse recovery and clear. Existing legacy write-lock directories do not prove their owner is dead and MUST NOT be blindly removed.

The writer records its transaction before creating a stage. It validates the candidate before moving the previous committed directory aside. Installing the candidate at the canonical path is the commit point. The persisted journal and surviving paths distinguish this point after local process termination. First-install staging is never committed merely because it is complete or valid.

Inspection reports committed data, unfinished work, cleanup residue and ownership separately. If interruption leaves the prior generation at its recorded previous path, that generation remains discoverable. Recognized work without committed data is interrupted, not absent. Cleanup residue beside a committed new generation does not mean the acquisition failed.

Recovery validates the committed generation before preserving or restoring it. It MUST NOT restore a partly deleted previous directory or guess among unjournaled candidates. Recovery retains the complete manifest, including publisher artifact identities and provider-specific source-vintage safeguards. Another download MUST refuse unresolved publication before source selection or transfer.

A precommit failure preserves the initiating exception and any restoration or cleanup exceptions. A postcommit cleanup failure retains the authoritative path, transaction identity and remaining paths in a distinct typed exception. Safe retry begins with inspection and recovery, not automatic removal of the only surviving store.

The configured cache root may resolve through a symlink at the public composition boundary. Managed provider directories, journals, ownership files and generation contents MUST NOT follow symlinks. Explicit clear removes terminal managed symlinks themselves, never their targets or unrelated siblings. All owned staging, workspace and preserved-download namespaces participate in lifecycle inspection and deletion. Workspace locations are resolved before source decoding. National preparation keeps the configured free-space minimum before acquisition. After transfer, it estimates additional growth from source counts and expanded source sizes before compilation and replay. It checks each filesystem that receives this growth. Existing inputs, the previous store and an existing candidate already reduce free space and MUST NOT be charged again. Sequential compilation and replay workspaces MUST NOT be added as if they coexist.

Poland keeps its ordering index in the managed workspace. Canada's source query can use native SQLite temporary files. Its admission check reconstructs default SQLite VFS routing only when SQLITE_TMPDIR and TMPDIR were set before process startup and remain unchanged for the process lifetime. SQLite can cache its initialization-time environment. The check cannot recover that state after late changes, so those sessions are unsupported even if their environment stays fixed during compilation. Restart Python with the intended environment before preparing Canada in such a session.

The check changes no environment variables or SQLite globals. Unix resolution follows SQLite's directory search; desktop Windows uses GetTempPathW, matching the reviewed SQLite 3.53.1 default VFS. Cygwin, UWP and custom VFS routing are not covered. SQLite global temp settings must remain unchanged during compilation.

Admission estimates are not reservations or guaranteed upper bounds. Later refusals identify the preparation phase; they MUST NOT claim that acquisition has not started. Late disk failure has the same preservation rules.

See National preparation measurements for measured build costs, resource use and verification limits.

The supported guarantee is local process interruption while the operating system and filesystem continue running. Tests use actual subprocess termination at persisted boundaries as well as injected exceptions and cleanup failures. These checks do not establish host or power-loss durability. Continuous reads during replacement, distributed locking and network-filesystem coordination are not promised.

The shared certification/publication entry point is the handoff for later provider build optimizations. Providers MUST NOT introduce another publication protocol.

docs.title: Daily streamflow for CAMELS-US gauges, 2015 to 2026
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

The CAMELS-US version 1.2 record lists time-series coverage through 31 December 2014. USGS publishes the same gauges' daily discharge up to the present, so you can pick up where CAMELS stops. This example downloads daily discharge from 1 January 2015 to 30 September 2026 for three CAMELS gauges in Maine and plots it.

The identifiers and names come from the CAMELS gauge list.

Station ID Name in CAMELS 01013500 Fish River near Fort Kent, Maine 01022500 Narraguagus River at Cherryfield, Maine 01030500 Mattawamkeag River near Mattawamkeag, Maine

docs.title: Download the data
docs.text:
Install RivRetrieve and matplotlib with uv add rivretrieve matplotlib. Run the Python blocks below in order in the same session. Retrieval needs network access but no credentials. Keep gauge identifiers as strings so their leading zeros survive.

find filters the packaged catalogue, pick keeps our three gauges and fetch downloads the days from start to end, both included. Leave end out to get everything up to the latest day USGS has published.

import rivretrieve as rr

gauges = rr.find(provider="usgs_nwis", quantity="discharge", frequency="daily", statistic="mean")
camels = rr.pick(gauges, station=["01013500", "01022500", "01030500"])
result = rr.fetch(camels, start="2015-01-01", end="2026-09-30")

print(result.issues)

Output:

()

Each row is one gauge and one day. The last rows:

print(result.data.select("station_id", "time", "value", "unit").tail(3))

Output:

shape: (3, 4)
┌────────────┬─────────────────────┬──────────┬──────┐
│ station_id ┆ time                ┆ value    ┆ unit │
│ ---        ┆ ---                 ┆ ---      ┆ ---  │
│ str        ┆ datetime[μs]        ┆ f64      ┆ str  │
╞════════════╪═════════════════════╪══════════╪══════╡
│ 01030500   ┆ 2026-09-28 00:00:00 ┆ 0.778713 ┆ m3/s │
│ 01030500   ┆ 2026-09-29 00:00:00 ┆ 0.818357 ┆ m3/s │
│ 01030500   ┆ 2026-09-30 00:00:00 ┆ 0.767387 ┆ m3/s │
└────────────┴─────────────────────┴──────────┴──────┘

USGS publishes these daily means; RivRetrieve does not calculate them from instantaneous observations. Values are converted from ft³/s to m³/s. Daily labels are plain calendar dates (time_zone="unknown"), so do not treat them as UTC.

docs.title: Check what came back
docs.text:
Print the dates before plotting. A gauge that stopped reporting looks the same as a quiet one on a plot.

import polars as pl

coverage = (
    result.data.group_by("station_id")
    .agg(
        pl.len().alias("days"),
        pl.col("time").min().dt.date().cast(pl.String).alias("first"),
        pl.col("time").max().dt.date().cast(pl.String).alias("last"),
    )
    .sort("station_id")
)
print(coverage.rows())

Output:

[('01013500', 4291, '2015-01-01', '2026-09-30'), ('01022500', 4291, '2015-01-01', '2026-09-30'), ('01030500', 4291, '2015-01-01', '2026-09-30')]

All three gauges have a value for every day from 2015-01-01 to 2026-09-30. For other gauges, compare days with the number of days between first and last. Missing days are not in the USGS record and are not filled in.

docs.title: Plot it
docs.text:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

names = {
    "01013500": "Fish River near Fort Kent",
    "01022500": "Narraguagus River at Cherryfield",
    "01030500": "Mattawamkeag River near Mattawamkeag",
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(10, 6.4), sharex=True)
for ax, (station, name) in zip(axes, names.items()):
    rows = result.data.filter(pl.col("station_id") == station).sort("time")
    ax.plot(rows["time"], rows["value"], lw=0.8)
    ax.set_title(f"{name}, Maine", loc="left", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
fig.supylabel("Discharge (m³/s)")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("camels_daily_discharge.png", dpi=150)

The figure above was made with this code (plus some styling, see docs/scripts/camels_example_plot.py) from a request on 5 October 2026.

docs.title: Gauge metadata
docs.text:
rr.metadata returns one row per gauge: name, coordinates, drainage area and more. It reads the packaged catalogue, so it works offline and needs no request. These are the columns you will use most. The wider table cells just keep the full names on one line.

meta = rr.metadata(camels)

with pl.Config(fmt_str_lengths=60, tbl_width_chars=140):
    print(meta.select("station_id", "station_name", "latitude", "longitude", "drainage_area_value", "drainage_area_unit"))

Output:

shape: (3, 6)
┌────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────┬────────────┬──────────────────────┬────────────────────┐
│ station_id ┆ station_name                                ┆ latitude  ┆ longitude  ┆ drainage_area_value  ┆ drainage_area_unit │
│ ---        ┆ ---                                         ┆ ---       ┆ ---        ┆ ---                  ┆ ---                │
│ str        ┆ str                                         ┆ f64       ┆ f64        ┆ list[str]            ┆ list[str]          │
╞════════════╪═════════════════════════════════════════════╪═══════════╪════════════╪══════════════════════╪════════════════════╡
│ 01013500   ┆ Fish River near Fort Kent, Maine            ┆ 47.2375   ┆ -68.582778 ┆ [""870"", ""870""]   ┆ ["sq mi", "sq mi"] │
│ 01022500   ┆ Narraguagus River at Cherryfield, Maine     ┆ 44.608056 ┆ -67.935278 ┆ [""227"", ""227""]   ┆ ["sq mi", "sq mi"] │
│ 01030500   ┆ Mattawamkeag River near Mattawamkeag, Maine ┆ 45.501111 ┆ -68.305833 ┆ [""1419"", ""1419""] ┆ ["sq mi", "sq mi"] │
└────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────┴────────────┴──────────────────────┴────────────────────┘

Latitude and longitude are in decimal degrees. The drainage area is in square miles, as USGS publishes it, and is stored as text, which is why it shows in quotes. USGS lists two area fields for these gauges and they agree. Elevation is also in the metadata, but USGS describes it as gage or land-surface altitude, so read station metadata before using it.

docs.title: Use it in your own study
docs.text:
Pass more gauge identifiers to pick and change the dates in fetch. Check result.issues and the dates per gauge before combining results with CAMELS. Before putting both on one axis, remember:

  • CAMELS and the numbers above both come from USGS, but CAMELS is a frozen version. USGS can revise past values, so the two can differ for the same day.
  • Recent values are provisional and USGS may revise them (see the provider page).
  • Check units and the daily time definition on both sides.

Save the table with result.data.write_parquet("usgs_daily.parquet"). To keep the source definitions, outcomes and provenance with it, use rr.to_bundle(result). The usage guide explains issues, time handling and cache reuse.

docs.title: Licence, citation and credit
docs.text:
USGS-produced data are in the U.S. Public Domain, so you can plot and share them, figures included. USGS asks for credit; see the USGS provider page for the wording.

The CAMELS version 1.2 record gives separate citations for the time series and catchment attributes. Cite the parts you use.

For streamflow and forcing time series:

  • Newman et al. (2014). A large-sample watershed-scale hydrometeorological dataset for the contiguous USA. UCAR/NCAR. doi:10.5065/D6MW2F4D
  • Newman et al. (2015). Development of a large-sample watershed-scale hydrometeorological dataset for the contiguous USA: dataset characteristics and assessment of regional variability in hydrologic model performance. doi:10.5194/hess-19-209-2015

For catchment attributes:

  • Addor et al. (2017). CAMELS: Catchment Attributes and MEteorology for Large-sample Studies. UCAR/NCAR. doi:10.5065/D6G73C3Q
  • Addor et al. (2017). The CAMELS data set: catchment attributes and meteorology for large-sample studies. doi:10.5194/hess-21-5293-2017

The observations retrieved here come from USGS, not from the CAMELS archive. Cite USGS and RivRetrieve as well.

docs.title: Verification evidence
docs.text: The private source archive maintains the retained-material inventory, collection identities, acquisition records, known gaps and archive tools. Its README gives access prerequisites and commands for discovery, exact retrieval, intake and publication. Use an explicitly reviewed archive revision and existing GitHub access. Runtime package users need no archive credentials.

docs.title: Obtain exact inputs
docs.text:
Select an exact collection from the archive. The archive tool checks release and asset identities, byte sizes, SHA-256 digests and extraction limits. For manifest-bound collections, it also checks the manifest and retained members. Download to a directory outside source checkouts, then pass the verified local input directory to the relevant verifier. Do not substitute a mutable latest release, search acquisition-machine paths or silently replace a selected input. Publishing archive material does not select it for a test or catalogue.

Collection integrity establishes which bytes were retrieved, not whether they support a source claim. Keep acquisition identities, original bytes, receipts and known limitations. A native-table rebuild cannot certify missing original responses. A later acquisition cannot replace an earlier one under its identity. Pinned fingerprints detect changed material; they do not prevent attachment loss or provide an independent backup.

docs.title: Verify source claims
docs.text:
RivRetrieve owns library behavior, catalogue transformations and their declarations. The private archive owns reviewed evidence ledgers, source-certification verifiers, retained source material and tests of its tooling. Tests and catalogue tools receive verified local inputs explicitly. Packaged catalogues remain in RivRetrieve and work without archive access. Historical provenance paths identify the original acquisitions; they do not locate files in the current checkout.

Catalogue publication receives an explicit selection of verified members and revision-pinned code references to their actual owning repositories. The selection records each adopted member's collection, manifest, artifact identity, digest, size and archive revision. The archive's material role and the member's use in the build remain separate. Adding a collection does not change a provider's selected inputs.

Use the private coordinator's catalogue-input mode for catalogue rebuild tests. Select the reviewed RivRetrieve revision and the independently reviewed archive code revision explicitly. Public builds and transformations use the RivRetrieve revision; private ledgers and verifiers use the archive code revision. Authored ledger inputs are verified separately from retained release members. Whole-file declaration references identify reviewed ledgers as well as Python declarations. A build's publication entry point is separate from the executable references for catalogue conversion, observation assembly and metadata projection. Authored constants retain their declaration reference without becoming automatic source derivations. The coordinator writes a restricted input handoff and an external product directory; builds do not write into the reviewed checkout. The build fixture selects the provider's declared native and recording support and verifies their exact local bytes. Only those adopted members enter packaged provenance. The full restricted receipt is not a package artifact.

Review the resulting station metadata, provenance, descriptors and distribution contents before copying approved products into RivRetrieve. New name mappings need both retained-input checks and a separate disclosure decision. Keep candidate field review and disclosure decisions separate from verification of adopted mappings. Compare existing area fields with their approved baseline without changing scalar values, units or absence states.

Use the private archive README to locate each provider's maintained checks:

  • Bosnia: complete baseline workbook checks require the controlled source bodies and receipts.
  • France: historical governing checks require the retained historical native table, not the current Hub’Eau catalogue table.
  • HydroPortail: native inventory rebuild and the limits of historical source witnesses.
  • ThaiWater: complete genuine-input verification must precede negative provenance regressions. The archive coordinator supplies the verified governing inputs after that positive check passes. A skipped test or an exception from missing files does not establish acceptance.
  • Brazil: digest-bound supporting inputs and retained recordings used by the offline rebuild.

docs.title: Run tests
docs.text:
The testing guide explains each layer's purpose, expected answers and ownership. Use it when adding or changing coverage.

Run source-independent checks from the RivRetrieve checkout without archive access:

uv run pytest --logic-only

Collection does not open private inputs. This route includes synthetic controls, packaged-catalogue checks and public declarations. It does not establish acceptance of genuine source inputs.

For retained-input tests, run the private archive coordinator from a clean, reviewed archive checkout. Authenticate with existing GitHub access. Both full commit IDs must identify independently reviewed code. Follow the archive README for restricted storage and execution prerequisites.

For example, the Canada HYDAT NO_DAYS checks use sparse SQLite row witnesses and separate publisher recordings. The reconstructed database is not a complete publisher artifact. Run those checks with:

uv run --isolated --locked python -B verify.py \
  --reviewed-archive-sha "$REVIEWED_ARCHIVE_SHA" \
  --code-checkout /path/to/reviewed-rivretrieve \
  --reviewed-code-sha "$REVIEWED_CODE_SHA" \
  --output "$NEW_PRIVATE_ACCEPTANCE_DIRECTORY" \
  --tests -- tests/test_ca_eccc_no_days_evidence.py

Use --tests -- tests for the whole test suite. Without --tests, the coordinator runs its full governing checks and fixed regression group. Selected tests declare the consumer paths they need; the private archive maps those paths to exact collection members. The coordinator acquires and verifies the selected inputs, runs required complete positive verifiers, then runs exactly the collected tests. No per-provider downloads or manual path configuration are needed. Missing access, missing material, changed bytes, changed test selection and skipped requested checks fail the controlled run.

Tests receive one repository-relative working copy through retained_evidence_root. RIVRETRIEVE_TEST_EVIDENCE_ROOT and THAIWATER_REVIEW_EVIDENCE_ROOT are internal coordinator handoffs, not proof of archive membership or normal developer setup. Tests do not acquire evidence or receive archive credentials. Detailed output, receipts, caches and temporary files remain in restricted storage. Review the safe summary before sharing it.

Test purposes remain distinct:

Selection What a passing check establishes --logic-only Source-independent behavior against synthetic controls or public package inputs -m recorded Parser or retrieval behavior against genuine retained recordings -m derived An offline rebuild or check of derived inputs, not the existence of original responses -m governing The specific catalogue or governing-source assertions in the selected checks -m live An observation of a live service, when such a check exists

Pass -m selections after -- in the archive command. Tests may have more than one purpose. A recording replay is not a live observation. Selecting a governing regression does not itself certify every source body; its declared full-positive prerequisites run first. Historical coverage gaps remain recorded in the archive.

Other provider checks and retained-input limits are recorded in the private archive. Its maintained README identifies the current provider instructions.

Run applicable full checks when governing claims, source bindings, verifiers or collections change. Missing mandatory material is blocked, not a passing or silently skipped check. Keep recording replay, native rebuilds, complete source-body verification and live-service observations distinct. Synthetic archive-mechanics tests do not establish genuine collection acceptance.

The private archive also maintains the full-check coordinator. It runs against an explicitly reviewed RivRetrieve commit and records exact collections, fingerprints, commands, outcomes, skips and limitations. Follow its current instructions rather than reconstructing a verification run from historical acceptance records.

docs.title: Rebuild Hub’Eau from original responses
docs.text:
The offline module rivretrieve._internal.providers.fr_hubeau.rebuild_catalogue reconstructs the native table and capture record, then publishes catalogue tables including station metadata. Follow the private archive README for the maintained command and reviewed input selection. Supply --input-receipt with the verified RetainedInputReceipt JSON, in addition to --build-inputs, --evidence-root, --availability-ledger, --revision, --out and --capture-output. The receipt selects the original site responses, their receipts, manifest and lineage. The adopted build inputs must include that support. Missing or changed members fail; the command does not fetch replacements.

Library callers of rebuild must now pass metadata_sources, obtained from read_station_metadata_sources with the verified input receipt and the declared Hub’Eau site pins. Include those sources when building the provenance used to select build_inputs. This also applies to callers that previously supplied only station responses. The retained native revision passed as revision remains separate from the reviewed executable revision.

Use a new output directory and a new capture path outside that directory. Existing destinations are refused to prevent replacement through file aliases. Keep both outside source checkouts and retained inputs. A later publication failure can leave the native table or capture record in the output location. Keep these candidates external until the complete build and source checks pass and their disclosure is approved.

docs.title: Protect controlled material
docs.text:
Run only reviewed code with private evidence or credentials. Tests receive local inputs, not archive credentials. Keep private bodies, request details, credentials and evidence-backed output out of public issues, assertion output, logs, caches, CI artifacts and distributions. Review summaries before sharing them. Downloading outside Git does not by itself prevent disclosure, and private archive access does not establish source-sharing rights.

Preserve originals and historical acceptance records. Retire redundant copies only after proving archive preservation and obtaining required owner approval. New provider code PRs carry code and exact archive references, not source corpora or private attachments. See the architecture for the runtime and catalogue boundaries.

docs.title: Publish a USGS catalogue
docs.text:
USGS discovery builds from complete modern time-series metadata and explicitly selected monitoring-location recordings. Supply --modern-metadata, --monitoring-locations (the archive's locations.json), --retention-manifest and --evidence-root. The retention declaration has schema_version: 2, historical_sources and agency-qualified retained_station_ids. Each historical source names a consumer_directory relative to the evidence root and its exact series_ids. Each series must resolve in its assigned source without overlapping current metadata. Original source acquisitions remain distinct.

Use --native-out to prepare the derived modern station table for archive adoption. It preserves modern names and WGS84 geometry; null geometry remains unknown. This table is a transformation of retained responses, not an original publisher table. Preparation and publication are separate operations.

Publication uses --out, --native, --legacy-native, --build-inputs, --acquisition-provenance and --evidence-root, in addition to the discovery inputs above. The publisher verifies the adopted modern and legacy byte identities, then compares the rebuilt modern projection with the adopted table. Legacy sitefile rows enrich matching agency-qualified identities with areas and USGS-issued elevations. They do not determine modern station availability. Historical NWIS series claims remain separate from executable modern series.

Library callers of write_catalogue supply the same reviewed graph, build inputs, modern native_table and separate legacy_table. They must pass verified inputs. Historical acquisitions and descriptors remain historical; retention does not assert current publication or observation availability.

docs.title: Behavior and changes
docs.text:
rr.download("pl_imgw") replaces the local store with a valid newly acquired history even when it ends earlier. Removed rows are not carried forward. Incomplete or ambiguous archive listings, failed transfers and invalid archives still prevent replacement. Canada's safeguard against an older dated release remains unchanged.

Preparation uses a smaller reconciliation journal, a temporary SQLite table that checks source-record and emitted-row coverage. Poland expands only the selected product during each product pass and uses 1024-row sort fetch chunks. An index maintained during scratch insertion avoids an implicit SQLite sort. Certification removes one redundant semantic scan, which checks stored values and schema, while retaining byte checks and complete independent source replay. These changes preserve the shared publication lifecycle.

docs.title: Method and exact revisions
docs.text:
Both versions use the same retained publisher inputs selected through the maintained verification archive. Builds ran serially with network access denied, using retained publisher originals. They used Python 3.13.14, Polars 1.40.1 and PyArrow 24.0.0 on Darwin 24.6.0 arm64, with 16 logical CPUs. Machine model and RAM were not recorded. Dependencies were locked at the executable revisions. Both versions compiled independent input copies named from publisher URL basenames.

  • Baseline: 30ee78e0f4dcb1b57508819894f6d82fbf980d6c.
  • Candidate: a906f8b7a1d14a05bc324ee331bc69115b35e7ca.
  • Reviewed archive executable: 53099b6bba902bf875b90d38eb22a6f8fd43994c.
  • Baseline harness SHA256: 04303bca6441142fc3e190354f4fc0f2db6d9d4ad73c0452b708504adb129d93.
  • Candidate harness SHA256: 339276768cb706f0a5a5e6e6c39e2498c9a7e4dd0ea4a40d536e820c420bae4b.

The baselines are fresh builds. Candidates replace audited prior stores linked to retained baseline copies. These hardlinks share the same underlying files (inodes). Compilation timers include certification, publication and cleanup, but exclude setup, working-copy preparation and postcheck hashes. Observer and extra-root monitoring overhead is unquantified. OS caches were not purged. Light synthetic checks and two brief, read-only ZIP-directory scans overlapped the Poland baseline. This was not an isolated benchmark.

docs.title: National results
docs.text:
Decimal GB and MB describe bytes. Five-second disk samples can miss short peaks.

Measure Poland baseline Poland candidate Canada baseline Canada candidate Local compilation, seconds 3,511.349 2,722.202 2,836.077 2,627.485 Observation rows 59,629,260 59,629,260 79,811,984 79,811,984 Partitions 228 228 344 344 Final store, MB 222.986 222.986 412.932 412.932 Sampled managed-file peak, GB 7.964 3.123 1.926 2.221 Sampled journal peak, GB 7.395 2.324 0.241 0.123 RSS high-water through compilation, GB 2.945 2.138 3.716 2.310

RSS includes imports, setup and candidate pre-audits. Its final sample precedes the later baseline-preservation post-audit and comparator. It is not the completed-job or system-wide peak. Smaller batches do not establish a total memory bound. The following timings are inclusive and overlapping; do not add them. Compile/write includes decoding, semantic validation and sealing. Source replay includes decoding and, in the baseline only, the redundant semantic scan.

Component, seconds Poland baseline Poland candidate Canada baseline Canada candidate Independent censuses 351.945 253.106 12.450 13.527 Sort preparation 1,714.493 1,185.489 not called not called Extraction preparation not called not called 4.105 4.830 Compile/write including seal 1,758.083 1,456.178 1,864.779 1,910.649 Source replay 1,399.013 1,010.100 952.094 696.517 Redundant certification scan 196.716 removed 262.310 removed

Poland still makes 6,954 raw decoder entries and 5,220 sort preparations. Smaller product expansion is protected by tests, not a separately measured national CPU saving. Canada still extracts four times. Its write phase increased; extraction remains a small cost. The candidate retains one complete semantic validation and independent replay. Remaining work is substantial; these timings promise no fixed speedup.

docs.title: Disk scope and admission limits
docs.text:
Old data, inputs, output and scratch coexist during replacement; renaming the old store creates no copy. Canada's higher managed peak includes its old 0.413 GB store. Poland's sampled active sorts were 393.839/403.218 MB: no sort-space reduction is shown. The historic 8.587 GB Polish journal is not the comparison baseline; artifact naming differed. Candidate simultaneous run-plus-originals-plus-baseline peaks were 3.660/3.242 GB for Poland/Canada by path, or 3.437/2.829 GB after counting each shared underlying file once. These are not physical APFS allocations. Separate component maxima are not simultaneous totals. Visible-file sampling misses open, unlinked SQLite spills; physical I/O was not measured.

Admission counts estimated additional growth on actual filesystems, excluding old stores and inputs already present. Here a source record is one Polish CSV row or one Canadian monthly table row. Calibration uses 160 bytes/source record for the journal, a 24-byte/output-row floor, Poland's 80-byte/source-record width reference and an excess-width term, plus explicit 64 MiB metadata headroom. Width/entropy probes inform these allowances; they are neither reservations nor guaranteed bounds. Downloads still buffer a complete response. SQLite caches and concurrent Python/Arrow buffers remain costs. Native temp accounting assumes the default VFS and unchanged startup environment. VFS means SQLite's operating-system file backend. Late environment changes and custom file backends are unsupported. Windows GetTempPathW has source review and synthetic controls, not native Windows execution evidence. Baseline TMPDIR preceded project imports; startup/site SQLite initialization was not established. The implementation changes no global temp settings.

docs.title: Acquisition replay and fidelity
docs.text:
Strict recorded replays passed: Poland's 943 GETs (76 listings, 867 ZIPs) took 0.209 s; Canada's 80 final-status HEAD probes and one GET took 0.156 s. Timers include provider discovery, on-demand retained-body reads and production transfer writes, excluding setup and identity hashes. Hash prechecks warmed files: these are local replay times, not network throughput or fresh acquisition. No missing HEAD payload/retry history was invented. Artifact URL/hash/size/vintage/order and complete response exhaustion matched.

Both national comparisons passed: all stored columns, including original source fields, matched across every row and partition. Schemas, floating-point bits and duplicate multiplicity matched in stored order. Manifests matched except actual build time. Original-seal byte/semantic audits and frozen input/code/receipt/archive postchecks passed. Baseline bytes, generation, inode and mtime were preserved; owned ctime changes were recorded. Synthetic tests protect omissions, substitutions, malformed sources, failed shorter refreshes, late resource failures and committed cleanup debt. No check infers withdrawal intent or live availability.

docs.title: Provider ports
docs.text:
Turn a source publication into a faithful RivRetrieve integration. Use the code requirements to guide research: the catalogue supports selection, provider code requests and reads source data, and the shared engine performs common operations.

Start from the relevant provider issue and current repository state. Treat earlier research and third-party adapters as leads to recheck, not authority for source meaning or current access. Identify the intended scope and the next unresolved step before investigating. Use the steps below for concrete outcomes and code references; read the references needed for the current work.

docs.title: Keep the provider ports tracker current
docs.text:
Check the provider ports tracker before selecting or starting a port. Confirm that the provider is not already implemented on main, marked in progress (🚧) by another contributor or agent, or listed in the externally blocked group awaiting an access or maintainer decision.

Update the tracker entry in place as work progresses. Fetch the latest issue body immediately before editing (for example with gh issue view 870 --json body) and change only that provider's line so concurrent updates are preserved:

  1. When starting work (beginning Step 1 research or creating a port/<provider> branch): change - [ ] to - [ ] 🚧 and append a short status note naming the active branch or Effort issue, such as *(in progress on port/ee-est, #352)*.
  2. When pausing on a blocker (such as awaiting an agency reply or a maintainer scope decision): keep 🚧 or move the entry to the blocked group and state what it is waiting on in the status note.
  3. When merged into main (after Step 8 final review is approved and the port pull request is merged into main, not when work finishes on a port/<provider> branch): remove 🚧, tick - [x], and record the merged pull request, such as *(merged in #900)*.

When opening a new provider-port issue that is not yet in the tracker, add a - [ ] entry in the matching complexity group linking to the new issue.

docs.title: Progress through evidence-backed steps
docs.text:
1. Establish source, scope and access.
  2. Establish the station catalogue and metadata.
  3. Establish series identity and physical meaning.
  4. Establish retrieval behavior.
  5. Integrate the supported scope with the shared engine.
  6. Verify the complete integration against genuine source evidence.
  7. Document supported behavior and limitations for users.

These steps organize progressive research and meaningful delivery outcomes. When planning a Program, use them as candidate Effort boundaries, adapting them to the actual provider rather than inventing work. Do not research or implement the whole port simply because this guide was read. Follow the user's requested scope and existing discovery, planning and review workflows. Reading this guide does not publish issues, contact an agency or authorize implementation.

Research thoroughly enough to defend each adopted claim. Recheck documentation, representative responses and relevant exceptions. Validate apparent inconsistencies before escalating them. Later findings can reopen an earlier conclusion. Evidence retention, tests and documentation develop throughout, not only in the final steps.

docs.title: Keep one continuing research record
docs.text:
Use the private verification-evidence repository for the provider's continuing research document and evidence. Find an existing record before creating another. Keep established findings, dated checks, supporting references, corrections, correspondence and open questions together across Efforts. For each material unknown, explain which implementation or user claim it affects.

Use the archive's existing intake and verification process for original material. The research document connects evidence; it does not replace original responses or certify a claim by recording it. Public issues carry safe summaries and handoffs. Keep private material and correspondence out of public code, issues and artifacts. Private storage does not establish permission to retain or disclose source material.

docs.title: Resolve or expose missing information
docs.text:
Investigate material gaps and prepare focused questions for the institution. Record what was checked, what was asked and any answer. Obtain authorization before sending correspondence. Do not treat silence as confirmation or require an answer to every question before any independent capability can proceed.

  • Proceed when required facts are established.
  • Preserve unknown facts when the engine can represent them honestly.
  • Pause an affected capability when proceeding would require guessing, such as assigning an unestablished quantity or unit, or claiming incomplete data is complete.
  • Distinguish a missing source fact from a limitation in the shared engine.

When investigation and correspondence cannot resolve a material blocker, present its consequences to the maintainer. The maintainer decides whether to narrow the scope, deliver a truthful limited capability, defer it or abandon it. Documentation cannot make an unsafe interpretation acceptable.

docs.title: Finish with a defensible result
docs.text: Account for the supported scope, evidence behind material claims, completed checks and remaining limitations. Use the existing testing guide and evidence guide, not a new verification system. Missing mandatory evidence blocks acceptance; it is not a passing check. Keep user documentation consistent with the delivered behavior. Stop at the requested handoff or review boundary.

docs.title: Provider steps and their code targets
docs.text: Paths below lead to the shared contracts and representative implementations. Inspect current code before copying a pattern. A working adapter is not evidence that its source interpretations apply to another publication.

docs.title: 1. Source, scope and access
docs.text:
Build toward: a provider declaration with the appropriate access kind, credentials and publication identity.

Establish who measures and publishes the data, relevant products and geographical scope, available routes, access conditions, terms and attribution. Obtain small genuine examples of metadata and observations. Distinguish unavailable access from an empty response and from evidence that has not yet been collected.

A terms or licence page that automated tools cannot read, such as one requiring JavaScript, is not the same as terms that do not exist. Ask a person to open it directly before drafting external correspondence; a publisher's own data catalogue often states a licence, in seconds, where a support request would take much longer.

ProviderDeclaration selects LiveStages for on-demand acquisition, BulkStore for explicit download and compilation, or CatalogueOnly for discovery without observation retrieval. “Live” includes historical service requests; it does not mean only current readings.

Outcome: a justified source and integration scope, with access and terms questions recorded. Reachability alone does not establish permission or physical meaning.

docs.title: 2. Station catalogue and metadata
docs.text:
Build toward: a reproducible catalogue builder and approved packaged artifacts that support offline discovery.

Establish station identifiers and their connection to observations, coordinates and reference systems, supported descriptive metadata and station-product associations. Check whether a field describes a station, sensor or series. Do not infer observation availability from a station listing or turn unknown coverage into a promise.

Use the catalogue schemas and publication path. The Lithuania builder illustrates provider, product, station and station-product tables. Descriptive station metadata and its supporting evidence are also published through the shared path.

Outcome: supported field mappings, catalogue coverage limits and original inputs needed to reproduce and verify the build. Missing optional metadata need not block retrieval; an unresolved station-to-observation relationship can.

docs.title: 3. Series identity and physical meaning
docs.text:
Build toward: definitions that connect source fields and published identities to RivRetrieve's physical facts without collapsing separate records.

Establish quantities, native units, distinct series, frequency, statistic, time information, vertical references, missing-value encodings and source statuses. Look for parallel series and real exceptions to proposed mappings. Do not interpret quality codes as a ranking or infer a daily mean from cadence or a field name alone.

SourceIdentity, PhysicalFacts and admission keep identity and physical interpretation separate. SeriesMapping can share supported mappings between catalogue publication and parsing; it is not a substitute for response-specific identities when the source requires them.

Preserve observation qualifiers, approval statuses, method notes, unmeasured source slots, and non-identity series attributes through declared AnnotationSchema definitions with plain Polars types, verified descriptions (never placeholders such as "unknown"), and official http or https reference_url links. Do not alter ObservationResult.data, create stream variants solely for annotation changes, or emit per-row informational quality-code issues when annotations carry those source fields.

Outcome: each adopted fact has supporting evidence, and remaining unknowns are explicit. Admission requires established quantity, source unit and valid conversion. Unknown time zone, temporal support or datum need not prohibit retrieval, but cannot satisfy filters or claims requiring those facts.

docs.title: 4. Retrieval behavior
docs.text:
Build toward: request rules and source acquisition that do not silently lose data.

Establish selectors, date boundaries, pagination, response caps, request limits, empty-response meanings, errors, rolling retention and revisions. Check that a successful response actually supports the claimed coverage. Preserve differences between published nulls, absent rows, empty answers and failed requests.

Providers declare windows through engine types. The shared planner prepares bounds; providers consume those bounds without shifting them. Provider stages exchange bytes, source-call origins, rows, identities, inventories, outcomes and issues. The Lithuania fetcher is a concrete example, not a universal source policy.

Outcome: a defensible acquisition contract, including failure and completeness limits. Identify necessary shared-engine changes rather than hiding them in source code.

docs.title: 5. Provider integration
docs.text:
Build toward: the agreed scope working through the public discovery and retrieval APIs.

Connect catalogue artifacts, configuration, request declarations, fetch/parse stages or bulk download/compile operations, and the provider declaration. Start with a representative end-to-end path and extend to the agreed products and real source differences. Develop focused tests alongside implementation. Return to research when code would otherwise encode an unsupported assumption.

The declaration example and manifest show registration. The parser example shows native parsing connected to source-series mappings. Canada's declaration shows the bulk alternative. Reuse shared conversion, clipping, assembly and storage.

Outcome: working provider behavior, including supported source failures alongside independent successful results. Registration alone is not a completed provider.

docs.title: 6. Verification
docs.text:
Build toward: evidence that both the code behavior and the adopted source meanings are correct within the stated scope.

Extend shared contracts and the all-provider catalogue rebuild. Use genuine retained responses for distinct supported routes and independently established expected results. Check identities, timestamps and values together. Verify relevant cache/store behavior, catalogue lineage and distribution contents.

When a suitable published observational dataset is available, usually a regional CAMELS dataset, require a bounded comparison with values retrieved through RivRetrieve's public API. Match stations confidently and select overlapping dates. Use a reproducible random sample without selecting for agreement; ten gauges is a useful default, not a rigid requirement. Plot both hydrographs with explicit unit conversion and preserved gaps. Inspect for obvious errors and investigate meaningful discrepancies without filtering, shifting or fitting values to force agreement.

A comparison window bounded to a published dataset's coverage, such as a CAMELS dataset's end date, is not evidence of the source's actual historical reach. Check each sampled station's own earliest-available-result metadata where the source publishes one, and test a genuine retrieval against a window near that claimed depth for at least one long-running station, not only the modern comparison window. A single failed attempt against a far-back window can be a transient, cold-query response rather than an absence of data; retry before concluding the data is not retrievable. Separately, a source may track an older, lower-frequency product (for example, manually-taken spot measurements) alongside the continuous product a provider retrieves, reaching further back than the continuous record does; note this as an open scope question when found, rather than assuming the continuous product's own history is the source's only route to older data.

Retain the dataset version, station and date selection, comparison method, figures, findings and limitations through the existing evidence process. If no suitable dataset is available, record why; that absence alone does not block the port. This is a sanity check alongside source verification, not proof of identical source definitions or independent measurement accuracy. Unresolved semantics remain caveats unless they make the comparison misleading.

Follow the testing and evidence guides. The private archive owns intake, retained inputs and source-certification tooling. Review exact code revisions before execution with private evidence. Synthetic tests, replay, derived rebuilds and live checks establish different things; none silently replaces another.

Outcome: an account of completed checks, exact supporting evidence and remaining limits. Missing mandatory genuine inputs block acceptance.

docs.title: 7. User documentation
docs.text:
Build toward: a provider page that explains the delivered capability with a verified practical example.

Explain who publishes the data, what users can retrieve, access requirements, source series distinctions, declared source-annotation schemas and fields where applicable, time and units, availability limits, terms and unresolved facts that affect interpretation. State consequences clearly rather than publishing the whole investigation. Keep detailed research and correspondence in the private record.

Follow documentation guidance and use existing provider pages for scope. Link general usage rather than repeat it. Do not present a successful example as proof of continuous coverage.

Reuse shared layout verbatim rather than inventing a new shape per provider. In particular, the "What you can retrieve" table uses this exact header, in every provider page that has one, whether or not the data needs every column:

| Quantity filter | Source field / `variant` | Frequency | Statistic | Source unit | Returned unit |

Before writing a new provider page, grep the other pages in ../providers/ for the section headers and table shapes you are about to use, and try hard to follow them. Existing pages already show how to handle a column that does not obviously apply: ba_fhmzbih fills Frequency/Statistic with Unknown rather than dropping the column. Difficulty fitting one provider's data into the shared shape is not by itself evidence that the shape is wrong; look for how another page handled a similar gap before concluding the table itself needs to change. If you still think it does, raise that for review rather than quietly adding, removing, or renaming a column on just the new page.

Outcome: users can understand the result and its limits without reconstructing the investigation. Documentation and implemented behavior agree.

docs.title: Preview the station explorer locally
docs.text: Preview the explorer inside the documentation, where its map fills the viewport below the documentation navigation. One compact panel holds Filtering, Selection and Python tabs. Other documentation pages keep their normal layout. The explorer uses the active documentation palette, including the existing scheme toggle; it has no separate theme control. The map opens around Switzerland without restricting provider filters or selecting gauges. Space beyond the basemap extent uses the documentation background color.

docs.title: Prepare and serve the documentation
docs.text:
Use Python 3.13 or later, uv, and Node.js 22.12 or later with npm. Run these commands from the repository root:

uv sync --all-extras --dev
uv run python docs/scripts/generate_station_catalogue.py
npm --prefix web/station-explorer ci
npm --prefix web/station-explorer run build
uv run mkdocs build --strict
uv run mkdocs serve -a 127.0.0.1:8000

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/map/. Keep the final command running during review; press Ctrl+C to stop it. These commands prepare and serve local files. They do not deploy the documentation.

The catalogue exporter reads approved packaged catalogue products and writes web/station-explorer/public/catalogue.json. It does not download national archives, retrieve observations, or require source credentials. Vite builds the browser app into docs/assets/station-explorer/ and copies the catalogue there. The documentation build requires both the prepared app and its catalogue. A missing asset stops the build with a preparation message; the build hook does not install frontend dependencies or run npm.

Repeat the catalogue export after catalogue changes. Repeat the frontend build after changing the app or exported catalogue, then restart the documentation preview if it has not reloaded. Generated catalogue files, browser bundles and the built site are local outputs, not source files to commit or review evidence.

docs.title: Review the request workflow
docs.text:
• Click a count bubble to zoom into its gauges. Groups split as projected points separate. Co-located markers spread out when clicked (MarkerCluster's spiderfy behavior), so each gauge remains inspectable. Selected gauges and conflicts remain separate map symbols.
  • Change discovery filters, inspect a gauge, and add it individually. Try Add all matches with a larger selection.
  • Set retrieval dates in Python, then inspect single-provider and multi-provider requests in Python. Changing dates must not change matches. Station identifiers must stay complete in copied code, including leading zeros.
  • Set quantity to discharge, add one station, then search for and add another. Change provider or use Clear search. Both selections and the discharge setting must remain unchanged.
  • Change the shared measurement settings. Incompatible selected gauges remain visible and block copying until those settings change or the gauges are removed.
  • Inspect Water body in gauge details. Norway 16.24.0 shows Mår · MÅRVATN; Switzerland 2004 shows Murtensee. Missing names show Not available.
  • Remove the final gauge. Copying executable code must remain blocked for an empty selection or invalid dates. Date errors also appear beside the inputs.
  • In the synthetic browser tests, selecting a catalogue-only provider must show an unsupported-retrieval warning and block copying without removing the selection.
  • Inspect bulk-download steps and credential-name comments in generated code. Do not execute national downloads or observation requests during local preview.
  • Compare this page with the Usage page to check that only the explorer uses the full-width layout. At 390 px, inspect a gauge and use Add gauge at the top of the panel. Hide the panel to reach covered map points. Try a long station selection.

Catalogue entries do not guarantee observations for a requested period, and counts need not represent unique physical sites across providers. Unknown availability is separate from a measurement-setting conflict. Unknown-CRS and NAD83 (EPSG:4269) coordinates are displayed on the WGS84 basemap without datum transformation. These are approximate display positions, not certified coordinates.

Provider and station controls browse gauges. Quantity, frequency, statistic and temporal support configure the requested observations for the entire selection and also narrow the map matches. Dates are retrieval settings, not catalogue coverage filters. Advanced physical and source-identity controls, series-fact details, and the general gauge list are not exposed in this iteration. Inspect individual gauges on the map; co-located gauges remain reachable through MarkerCluster spiderfy.

The snapshot has 75,270 catalogue entries, of which 74,115 have matching series. Entries without described series are not individually browsable in this reduced UI. This catalogue limit does not establish absence of observations.

Python previews use Shiki with the official VS Code Light+ and Dark+ themes, selected by the documentation scheme. The preview shows at most ten station IDs; copying returns every selected gauge in complete plain Python. Shortened previews contain non-executable omission markers. Unresolved requests remain commented and cannot be copied. Normal multi-provider requests use one combined selection and fetch_by_provider. Provider-specific requests preserve exact pairs whenever a combined provider/station selection would include other pairs, including pairs that could appear in a later catalogue.

docs.title: Basemap configuration
docs.text:
For local CARTO tiles, configure VITE_CARTO_BASEMAP_API_KEY in web/station-explorer/.env.local, which Git ignores. Use a project-owned public client key under CARTO's basemap terms. Rebuild the frontend after changing the configuration. Vite embeds VITE_ values in browser bundles by design; this key is public, not a server credential. Do not commit the configuration or include keys or keyed tile URLs in review artifacts.

With a key configured, the existing documentation scheme selects CARTO Positron (light_all) or Dark Matter (dark_all) automatically. Without a local key, the map uses OpenStreetMap. Tile failures do not add a banner; browser checks retain sanitized diagnostics without keyed request URLs. Restrict the key to approved localhost and production hosts, check account quotas, and retain CARTO and OpenStreetMap attribution. Report rejected hosts rather than removing restrictions.

The documentation workflows map the repository secret CARTO_BASEMAP_API_KEY to VITE_CARTO_BASEMAP_API_KEY during the frontend build and fail if it is missing. The build embeds that public client key; visitors do not need individual keys. Relevant changes on main trigger a documentation build check without deployment. Documentation deploys only after a published release succeeds on PyPI.

The browser handoff ends at Python code. It does not execute that code or collect credentials. Background map tiles may use the basemap service; they are not observation requests. Automated checks do not establish responsiveness or finish the owner's hands-on review. Report usability problems and stop for feedback.

docs.title: Source-independent checks
docs.text:
npm --prefix web/station-explorer test
npm --prefix web/station-explorer exec -- playwright install chromium
npm --prefix web/station-explorer run test:browser

With the MkDocs preview running, check the full catalogue inside the docs:

DOCS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 npm --prefix web/station-explorer run test:browser

The last command measures initial loading, filtering, and adding a long selection. It checks that the explorer requests only localhost and basemap tiles. The existing documentation theme also requests Google fonts and GitHub repository metadata. It does not contact observation services or run generated retrieval code.

docs.title: Swiss observation series definitions
docs.text:
ch_foen.official_series.source_series resolves official API coordinates and already established unit bindings. Catalogue generation uses this entry point; observation parsing can use it without fetching data or loading configuration. The provider uses these definitions for official discovery and retrieval.

Identity uses the station string, route, parameter and raw tsName. Keep leading zeros, unsuffixed and _01 names, and archive/recent publications separate. The recent feed has no raw series name. Distinct native units produce separate physical fact segments, not new series identities. Changed knowledge does not rename a series. A catalogue association is a witness, not a complete inventory or record boundary, including when its observed values are all null.

docs.title: Physical facts
docs.text:
Archive unit bindings come from the published unit fields. Recent bindings come from station-page parameter labels; missing labels remain unknown. Shared admission converts native scales dimensionally. Above-sea-level labels establish a reference, not a named per-series datum. The historical 2282 archive Q/W units are m³/s and metres above sea level; its recent labels are independently bound. No 890 m offset or network-wide unit assumption is applied.

Ordinary ten-minute/hourly archive products are interval means. Daily, monthly and yearly products describe calendar windows beginning at midnight in fixed UTC+1. Minimum/maximum statistics describe extrema of short-term measurements, not daily means. Their temporal_support describes the aggregate window; the underlying measurement's averaging duration and the time of the extreme remain unknown. No averaging algorithm or missing-input threshold is assumed.

Timestamp serialization remains UTC. day_definition="UTC+01:00" describes the aggregation calendar, and timestamp_anchor="start" describes the aggregate label. Request planning and clipping use the established aggregate calendar while preserving UTC labels. A bare-date request includes the first and last aggregate day, including their preceding-date 23:00 UTC labels. Calendar periods are not fixed 30-day months or 365-day years:

Aggregate UTC interval (start included, end excluded) February 2025 2025-01-31 23:00 to 2025-02-28 23:00 February 2024 2024-01-31 23:00 to 2024-02-29 23:00 Year 2024 2023-12-31 23:00 to 2024-12-31 23:00 1 July 2025 2025-06-30 23:00 to 2025-07-01 23:00

Shared request planning, subdivision, clipping and cache handling preserve these calendar boundaries. Do not classify February's label as January from its UTC date or relabel its clock value as UTC+1.

Recent timestamps mark measurement end. Exact per-series averaging durations remain unknown; cadence does not establish them. At station 7008, MonatsMittel_Orbe_flex in data_1day_mean retains unknown statistic, frequency, support and anchor. Neither its route, name nor cadence supplies those facts. Its units and UTC timestamps can still be preserved. Optional unknowns do not prevent admission, but cannot satisfy filters requiring established facts.

docs.title: Parser handoff
docs.text:
Keep null values, zero, absent rows and failed requests distinct. These definitions do not parse or replace observation values. The official parser preserves archive releaseState in annotation schema ch_foen.archive and recent releaseStatus in ch_foen.recent, keeping explicit nulls and native types distinct from 0. RELEASE_STATUS_MEANINGS records publisher vocabulary separately: null and 0 mean raw, 1 unreleased/prechecked, 2 released/checked and 3 released/definitive. Status 3 includes corrections from status 2 and definitive stage–discharge relations. This is not a quality ranking or filtering policy. The unresolved word ersetzt does not establish replacement lineage.

Catalogue temporal facts require source.product.temporal_meaning in the selected provenance. The private archive owns the supporting originals and reviewed source checks. Synthetic tests protect the definitions' behavior; genuine-input checks and disclosure review are required before publishing rebuilt catalogue products.

docs.title: Choosing useful tests
docs.text: Every test protects a named promise, uses an expectation that can detect the claimed defect, and runs at the simplest level that can expose it. Providers share this model. Source differences justify focused exceptions.

docs.title: Choose the level
docs.text:
Level Useful proof Expected answer Small synthetic example A conversion, parser rule, invariant or failure boundary An explicit value or independently constructed invalid input Shared library contract Engine, catalogue, transport, store or public API behavior Handwritten rows, identities, states and errors Retained response replay A provider handles the selected publisher response Independently read source fields and values Native-input rebuild The assembled catalogue path reproduces the approved product Reviewed packaged tables and source declarations Independent source check A particular interpretation agrees with retained source material Original bodies, publisher receipts and reviewed source controls Installed distribution The built package works offline and excludes private material Public behavior and explicit permitted package contents Live observation A publisher service behaved that way at that time The request and response recorded for that observation

A successful rebuild from a derived table does not prove that its originals exist. Replay does not establish current service availability. A round trip can prove preservation or encoding consistency; it cannot establish the correctness of the source interpretation used on both sides.

docs.title: Make the expectation independent
docs.text:
Use a small calculation when it fully describes the promise. This synthetic coordinate example checks arithmetic and the converter's declared sign convention:

import pytest

from rivretrieve._internal.providers.za_dws.generate_catalogue import (
    convert_unsigned_dms_coordinates,
)

coordinates = convert_unsigned_dms_coordinates(
    "25:30:00", "28:15:00", station_id="example"
)

assert coordinates == pytest.approx((-25.5, 28.25))

It does not verify the contents of an original DWS PDF. That claim needs the original material and its source-specific check.

For recorded observations, compare timestamps and values together. Sorting the values alone can miss values attached to the wrong time. Include the source-series identity when several series share a timestamp. Use library frame assertions for whole tables. Keep units, unknowns, null values, absent rows and failed requests distinct in expected results.

A historical snapshot can remain an independent regression control when its reviewed source facts and order are still intentional promises. State that role. Do not calculate a replacement expectation with the transformation being tested. Test historical readability separately from the current package interface.

docs.title: Share contracts without hiding source differences
docs.text:
The shared all-provider catalogue rebuild in tests/test_catalogue_origin_certification.py exercises each real publication entry point with selected inputs. It checks offline operation, unchanged inputs, output completeness, source identity and approved catalogue contents. Add a new provider there rather than copying a second successful national rebuild.

A shared small test covers each origin-validation rule. One negative build per provider or distinct partition proves that the generator calls that validation. A full national build for every missing column repeats the same local rule.

Retain focused provider checks for real differences such as native units, timestamp labels, pagination, source quality vocabulary, identity fields and coordinate interpretation. Keep a positive replay for each distinct published route. Generic malformed-input cases usually belong beside the parser or shared validator, with one assembled check where failure propagation adds a separate promise.

A negative test must reach the rule it names. Start from a valid input. For a relation-validation test, update unrelated byte identities when necessary to get past the byte-integrity check. For a corruption test, leave those identities unchanged. Eleven ledger edits rejected by the same digest check prove one digest boundary, not eleven field validators.

docs.title: Keep setup isolated
docs.text:
Use temporary cache and store roots. A public fetch test must not read a contributor's compiled store. Keep registry and monkeypatch state local to each test. Share expensive unchanged package inputs only through the existing detached, fingerprint-aware fixtures. Changed or corrupt files must still reach validation.

Reuse the existing installed wheel and sdist-wheel fixtures. Under pytest-xdist, workers share one read-only wheel and sdist-wheel build per test run, while each verification process gets a separate working directory and home. Keep planted-file exclusion checks: inspecting a clean package alone cannot prove that private files would be excluded from a build.

Do not add a second validator, downloader, fixture registry or test coordinator. A helper should remove repetition without making a parallel implementation of the behavior it claims to test.

docs.title: Keep ownership and acceptance clear
docs.text:
RivRetrieve owns library behavior and catalogue transformations. It keeps small synthetic fixtures, approved runtime products and safe support references. The private archive owns acquisition, retention and controlled verification mechanics, including nested-package byte checks. Outer archive integrity does not replace checks of inner members or publisher receipts.

Run source-independent checks with:

uv run pytest --logic-only

To run source-independent checks across multiple worker processes:

uv run pytest --logic-only -n auto --dist worksteal

Tests that consume retained material declare exact consumer scopes and their purpose. Use the existing private coordinator to select verified inputs and run required complete positive checks before the related negative regressions. See Verification evidence for commands, review requirements and private-output rules. Missing mandatory inputs block acceptance; they are never silently skipped or replaced by synthetic data.

When changing tests, explain the defect protected by each new case and where a removed case's useful guarantee goes. Exact prose, private helper names and file layout need checks only when they are intentional contracts. Measure expensive changes against the same selected suite, Python version and isolation conditions. Report interrupted runs and unavailable evidence separately from passing results.

docs.title: Argentina: INA (Alerta5)
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider ar_ina Country Argentina (plus one binational Río Uruguay border gauge in Uruguay) Published by Instituto Nacional del Agua (INA), Subgerencia de Sistemas de Información y Alerta Hidrológico (SIyAH), with federated national, binational, provincial and municipal networks Read from Official INA Alerta5 REST API (alerta.ina.gob.ar/a5) Quantities Discharge, stage Stations in the catalogue 829 river gauges. Availability depends on station, quantity, series and period Station metadata Station name and water-body name. See Fields by provider Credentials None Licence stated by Argentina.gob.ar Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (Creative Commons Atribución 4.0 Internacional, CC BY 4.0); source attribution required Agency documentation INA Alerta Hidrológico, Alerta5 portal, Alerta5 OpenAPI specification, Punctual series guide

Retrieve four days of daily mean discharge at station 8, Andresito on the Iguazú River:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="ar_ina",
    station="8",
    quantity="discharge",
    frequency="daily",
    statistic="mean",
)

result = rr.fetch(selection, start="2024-01-01", end="2024-01-04", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print([(issue.severity, issue.code) for issue in result.issues])

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2024-01-01T03:00:00.000000,+00:00,839.95,m3/s
2024-01-02T03:00:00.000000,+00:00,898.63,m3/s
2024-01-03T03:00:00.000000,+00:00,2051.27,m3/s
4
[('info', 'provenance.citation_not_established')]

The request returned four published daily means in m³/s. The preview shows the first three days. Each Argentine calendar day since March 2009 begins at local midnight in UTC-03:00, so 1 January's daily mean is labelled 2024-01-01T03:00:00.000000 with time_zone="+00:00"; see Time and data status for historical Daylight Saving Time periods.

The informational issue provenance.citation_not_established means the packaged provider catalogue has no fixed verbatim citation string configured. It does not mean retrieval failed or that attribution is optional; follow the attribution requirements in Terms and citation.

cache="bypass", the default for live rr.fetch calls, requests Alerta5 directly without reading or writing a local cache. Passing cache="reuse" stores retrieved observations locally so later requests for already-covered dates reuse the local store. This output was checked live on 2026-11-09. Source records can be updated or revised over time. See Usage for selection options and working with returned data.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
Argentina's National Water Institute (Instituto Nacional del Agua, INA), through its Hydrological Information and Warning Systems Sub-directorate (Subgerencia de Sistemas de Información y Alerta Hidrológico, SIyAH), publishes national and Cuenca del Plata river observations through the Alerta5 service. Alerta5 aggregates gauge measurements collected by several operating networks, so appearance on Alerta5 does not mean that INA operates every station itself. The 829 river gauges in RivRetrieve's packaged catalogue belong to nine source networks:
