Source network in Alerta5 Stations Red Hidrológica Nacional, telemetric network (sat2, SSRH) 479 Red Hidrológica Nacional, historical database (alturas_bdhi, SSRH) 235 Prefectura Naval Argentina staff gauges (alturas_prefe) 88 INA Delta and Greater Buenos Aires network (ina_delta) 16 Salto Grande binational dam hydrometeorological network (estaciones_salto_grande) 4 Nucleoeléctrica Argentina (na-sa) 3 Municipality of Quilmes (quilmes) 2 INTA Delta (inta_delta) 1 Comisión Administradora del Río Uruguay (alturas_varios, station 1699 Nueva Palmira) 1

No API key or account is required. RivRetrieve searches the packaged station and series catalogue offline; rr.fetch then requests JSON observations over HTTPS from Alerta5. Station identifiers are integer Alerta5 station IDs kept as strings, such as "8" or "1967". When the same physical river location has entries in more than one contributing network (for example a telemetric sat2 entry alongside a historical alturas_bdhi entry), Alerta5 assigns each network entry its own station ID, and RivRetrieve keeps them separate.

The packaged ar_ina catalogue covers physical river and inland-delta gauges with observed discharge or stage records:

  • 828 gauges carry EPSG:4326 coordinates, and 1 river gauge ("96", Colorado on the Bermejo River) is retained with null latitude and longitude because Alerta5 publishes its stage series without station coordinates.
  • Inland Paraná Delta and freshwater inner Río de la Plata gauges (such as Tigre, San Fernando, Buenos Aires, and La Plata in alturas_prefe, and urban Greater Buenos Aires stream gauges in ina_delta) and the shared Río Uruguay border gauge 1699 (Nueva Palmira, Uruguay, operated by CARU) are included.
  • Virtual hydrological-model nodes, model simulations, forecasts, climatologies, and interpolated or derived analysis series stored in Alerta5 alongside gauge measurements are excluded; RivRetrieve admits only direct measurement (medición directa) and rating-curve (curva de gasto) observational procedures.
  • Maritime and outer-estuary coastal tide-gauge networks (Servicio de Hidrografía Naval estaciones_shn and PVNyMM estaciones_pvnymm), sparse manual field discharge gaugings (aforos), and groundwater phreatic wells are excluded.
  • Surface-water temperature has only two empty placeholder entries in Alerta5 with no observations, so ar_ina exposes discharge and stage only.

Argentina's Subsecretaría de Recursos Hídricos (SSRH) also operates a separate federal hydrological portal (SNIH) with additional historical discharge, stage, and water-temperature records; a separate provider for SNIH is tracked in #729.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Alerta5 publishes five observational river discharge series types and eight observational river stage series types:

Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge Qmd (Caudal medio diario; per-series ID in variant) Daily Mean m^3/s m³/s discharge Q (Caudal; per-series ID in variant) Unknown Instantaneous m^3/s m³/s discharge Qmm (Caudal medio mensual; per-series ID in variant) Monthly Mean m^3/s m³/s discharge Qmmin (Caudal mínimo mensual; per-series ID in variant) Monthly Minimum m^3/s m³/s discharge Qmmax (Caudal máximo mensual; per-series ID in variant) Monthly Maximum m^3/s m³/s stage Hmd (Altura hidrométrica media diaria; per-series ID in variant) Daily Mean m m stage H (Altura hidrométrica; per-series ID in variant) Unknown Instantaneous m m stage H1h (Altura hidrométrica horaria; per-series ID in variant) Hourly Unknown m m stage Hm4h (Altura hidrométrica 4-horaria; per-series ID in variant) Unknown Unknown m m stage Hms (Altura hidrométrica media semanal; per-series ID in variant) Unknown Mean m m stage Hmm (Altura hidrométrica media mensual; per-series ID in variant) Monthly Mean m m stage Hmmin (Altura hidrométrica mínima mensual; per-series ID in variant) Monthly Minimum m m stage Hmmax (Altura hidrométrica máxima mensual; per-series ID in variant) Monthly Maximum m m

Discharge in m^3/s and stage in m require no numerical scaling; RivRetrieve normalises the discharge unit label to m3/s while keeping "m^3/s" in source_unit. It does not calculate daily or monthly aggregates from sub-daily readings or merge separate series.

Availability varies substantially across stations. In the packaged catalogue snapshot (2,611 witnessed station-series pairs across 829 gauges), instantaneous stage (H) is listed at 808 stations and daily mean stage (Hmd) at 756, whereas daily mean discharge (Qmd) is listed at 82 stations, instantaneous rating-curve discharge (Q) at 32, 4-hourly stage (Hm4h) at 391, hourly stage (H1h) at 3, and weekly mean stage (Hms) at 32. A station being listed in the catalogue does not guarantee observations for every quantity or requested period.

Each published Alerta5 time series has its own numeric Alerta5 series ID, which RivRetrieve exposes as variant (for example variant="26605" for daily mean discharge at station "8"). Unlike providers with named processing levels, these numeric IDs belong to individual station series rather than forming a provider-wide menu. Within the packaged river catalogue, each station has at most one observational series per row in the table above.

Several stage series have Unknown in Frequency or Statistic:

  • Hourly (H1h) and 4-hourly (Hm4h) stage: Alerta5 declares 1-hour and 4-hour time steps with a Continuous data type rather than Average. Comparing overlapping observations shows that these series place a single stage reading onto each 1-hour or 4-hour slot rather than averaging readings across the slot. RivRetrieve sets frequency="hourly" on H1h, leaves frequency unknown on Hm4h (4-hourly is not a named filter in RivRetrieve's frequency vocabulary), and leaves statistic unknown on both so mean and instantaneous filters do not select them by mistake.
  • Weekly mean stage (Hms): Summarises 7-day Monday-to-Monday intervals with statistic="mean". Because RivRetrieve's frequency filter vocabulary has daily and monthly rather than weekly, frequency remains unknown.
  • Instantaneous discharge (Q) and stage (H): Match statistic="instantaneous" without a frequency filter because telemetry and staff-gauge reporting intervals vary across stations and periods (from 10- or 15-minute automatic transmissions to daily or sub-daily manual readings).
  • Monthly minimum and maximum series (Qmmin, Qmmax, Hmmin, Hmmax): Report the minimum or maximum of the station's underlying observations within each calendar month, stamped at the start of the month.

Inspect all candidate series and station metadata at a gauge offline before fetching, and use rr.pick(..., variant=...) (or frequency="hourly" for H1h) when targeting a series whose frequency or statistic is unknown:

station_52 = rr.find(provider="ar_ina", station="52", quantity="stage")
candidates = rr.series(station_52)
metadata = rr.metadata(station_52)

hourly_stage = rr.pick(station_52, variant="31605")

docs.title: Stage references and station metadata
docs.text:
River stage (altura hidrométrica) in Alerta5 is measured in metres relative to each station's local staff-gauge zero (cero de escala). RivRetrieve sets vertical_reference="gauge_zero" and leaves vertical_datum unknown on all stage series. Water levels below local gauge zero are physically valid during low-water periods and remain negative (for example -0.27 m in monthly minimum stage at station 8, Andresito). Do not compare raw stage values across different gauges as elevations above sea level.

Station metadata from rr.metadata(selection) exposes two native fields from Alerta5:

  • nombre as station_name (populated for all 829 river gauges), and
  • rio in water_body_name_value (populated for 353 gauges and null at the remaining 476 gauges where Alerta5 leaves rio empty).

Both drainage_area_* and elevation_* columns are null (state="no_metadata" in rr.metadata(selection, view="source")):

  • Alerta5's station inventory does not publish catchment areas, and its optional basin-polygon endpoint covers fewer than 3% of river gauges while mixing total drainage basins with incremental model subcatchments and zero placeholders.
  • An optional cero_ign attribute in Alerta5 (73 river gauges) records the height of the local staff-gauge zero relative to Argentina's Instituto Geográfico Nacional (IGN) datum rather than ground elevation, while a sparse altitud attribute (10 river gauges) states neither a unit nor a vertical datum. Neither field is exposed as station ground elevation.

docs.title: Time and data status
docs.text:
Alerta5 returns all observation timestamps in UTC (...Z). RivRetrieve preserves those UTC timestamps with time_zone="+00:00" (time_zone="UTC" in rr.series(...)), and rr.to_utc(result) returns them unchanged.

Pay attention to local civil midnight when aligning daily, weekly, or monthly aggregates with calendar dates:

  • March 2009 to present (UTC-03:00): Argentina has observed fixed UTC-03:00 without Daylight Saving Time since March 2009. Daily, weekly, and monthly intervals begin at 00:00 local time, which appears as 03:00:00 UTC (for example 2024-01-01T03:00:00.000000 for 1 January 2024).
  • Pre-2009 Daylight Saving Time transitions (UTC-02:00 in summer): During historical Argentine summer-time periods (such as October 2008 to March 2009), local midnight fell at 02:00:00 UTC (UTC-02:00). In Alerta5's database, the spring transition day spans 23 hours (03:00:00 UTC to the next day's 02:00:00 UTC), summer days begin at 02:00:00 UTC, and the autumn transition day spans 25 hours (02:00:00 UTC to 03:00:00 UTC). Because the UTC offset of local midnight shifts across historical DST years, RivRetrieve leaves day_definition unknown rather than claiming a fixed UTC offset across all decades.

On daily, weekly, monthly, hourly, and 4-hourly series, time marks the start of the interval (timestamp_anchor="start"). On instantaneous discharge (Q) and stage (H), time marks the measurement instant (timestamp_anchor="measurement_time"), including exact sub-minute telemetry timestamps (such as :10 seconds) where recorded by automatic loggers.

Alerta5 serves operational real-time telemetry and historical gauge archives through the same API without per-observation quality-assurance flags. It does publish a series-level operational-availability code (H, C, RT, NRT, S, and the H+S/C+S/RT+S/NRT+S combinations, or N for no observations available), documented on the a5-portal-home map. RivRetrieve keeps the default series frame unchanged and preserves that code as a series-scope annotation, under schema ar_ina.series:

Field Type data_availability String

Inspect it alongside the series it describes:

print(rr.annotations(result).select("schema", "name", "dtype", "row_count").write_csv(), end="")

annotated = rr.series(result, annotations=True).select("series_id", "variant", "data_availability")
print(annotated.write_csv(), end="")

Output:

schema,name,dtype,row_count
ar_ina.series,data_availability,String,1
series_id,variant,data_availability
820d18989de6cb74eadc27b5686a24a8d09a051623953639e98272cd22e1fc4c,26605,NRT

Station 8's daily mean discharge series (variant="26605") carries NRT (near-real-time) as its data_availability code. This output was checked live on 2026-11-17.

This describes operational feed latency, not a data validation grade, and RivRetrieve makes no quality judgement of its own. RivRetrieve issues a targeted series-lookup request to harvest it even for a station already established from the packaged catalogue, so it is not tied to needing that lookup to resolve series identity. If that request fails, or the publisher's response omits the code, the annotation is simply absent for that series and an informational source.annotation_unavailable issue is recorded; this never blocks or invalidates the observation rows themselves.

Keep missing-data cases distinct when inspecting results:

  • Missing dates or sub-daily gaps in Alerta5 generally produce no observation rows rather than null placeholders. RivRetrieve requests stored database observations only (suppressing Alerta5's synthetic regular-grid boundary nulls) and does not fill missing time steps.
  • Where Alerta5 stores an explicit database record whose value is null, RivRetrieve omits that gap marker and records an informational source.gap_marker issue in result.issues.
  • Long retrieval windows are split automatically into bounded requests (at most 365 days per request for sub-daily and slotted stage or instantaneous discharge, and at most 3,650 days per request for daily and weekly series) and assembled without boundary duplicates. Check issues whenever a request returns fewer rows than expected.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
INA's Alerta Hidrológico portal is published on Argentina's national argentina.gob.ar platform, whose terms and conditions license public content under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) (Creative Commons Atribución 4.0 Internacional) unless otherwise stated. Reuse requires attribution to the source.

Both rr.describe("ar_ina") and result.provenance expose license="Creative Commons Atribución 4.0 Internacional", while citation is omitted from rr.describe("ar_ina") and None on result.provenance (because argentina.gob.ar states general CC BY 4.0 attribution obligations rather than prescribing a single verbatim citation string, which also produces the informational provenance.citation_not_established issue during rr.fetch). When publishing or redistributing retrieved data, credit the Instituto Nacional del Agua (INA), Subgerencia de Sistemas de Información y Alerta Hidrológico (https://alerta.ina.gob.ar/a5), name the contributing monitoring network where applicable (such as Subsecretaría de Recursos Hídricos, Prefectura Naval Argentina, CARU, or Salto Grande), and record the station ID, series variant ID, requested period, and retrieval date.

RivRetrieve paces live requests politely (at most two requests per second) and reuses locally cached observations when cache="reuse" is passed.

docs.title: Austria: eHYD
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider at_ehyd Country Austria Published by Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Climate and Environmental Protection, Regions and Water Management (BMLUK), Department I/3 Water Balance (HZB), with provincial hydrographic services Read from Official eHYD web services (ehyd.gv.at) Quantities Discharge, stage, water temperature Stations in the catalogue 746 river gauges (744 with selectable series). Availability depends on station, quantity, product and period Station metadata Station name, water-body name and drainage area. See Fields by provider Credentials None Licence stated by BMLUK Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0); source attribution required (Datenquelle: ehyd.gv.at) Agency documentation eHYD portal, General guide, Current telemetry guide

Retrieve one week of validated daily mean discharge at station 209486, Böheimkirchen on the Perschling:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="at_ehyd",
    station="209486",
    quantity="discharge",
    frequency="daily",
    statistic="mean",
)

result = rr.fetch(selection, start="2023-01-01", end="2023-01-07", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print(result.issues)
print(rr.series(result, annotations=True)["data_quality"].to_list())

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2023-01-01T00:00:00.000000,unknown,0.112,m3/s
2023-01-02T00:00:00.000000,unknown,0.107,m3/s
2023-01-03T00:00:00.000000,unknown,0.109,m3/s
7
()
['Geprüfte Daten']

The request returned seven published daily means in m³/s from eHYD's validated historical archive (owf_abfl_tagesmittel). The preview shows the first three days, and rr.series(result, annotations=True) shows the archive's Geprüfte Daten label from at_ehyd.series. time_zone is unknown because the exported CSV files do not state a UTC offset; see Time and data status. The empty tuple () means this retrieval reported no transport, parsing, or gap-marker issues. Attribution is still required when using the data; see Terms and citation.

cache="bypass", the default for live rr.fetch calls, requests eHYD directly without reading or writing a local cache. Passing cache="reuse" stores the station's downloaded archive series locally so later historical queries for the same gauge and product reuse the cached series without downloading the full CSV file again. This output was checked live on 2026-11-03. Published values can change across hydrographic yearbook revisions. See Usage for selection options and result handling.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
Austria's Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Climate and Environmental Protection, Regions and Water Management (Bundesministerium für Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Klima- und Umweltschutz, Regionen und Wasserwirtschaft, BMLUK), Department I/3 Water Balance (Wasserhaushalt, formerly the Hydrographic Central Office, HZB), publishes national hydrographic data through eHYD. Measurements are collected and validated in cooperation with the nine provincial hydrographic services (Hydrographische Landesdienste), the waterway operator viadonau on the Danube, and municipal water services. Appearance on eHYD does not mean that BMLUK operates every station itself.

No API key or account is required. RivRetrieve searches the packaged station and series catalogue offline; rr.fetch then requests data directly from eHYD's public web services. Station identifiers are six-digit HZB numbers (hzbnr), kept as strings such as "209486".

The packaged at_ehyd catalogue covers flowing surface waters only: 746 river gauges in EPSG:4326, of which 744 expose at least one selectable discharge, stage, or water temperature series (2 river gauges, 207480 and 230102, publish only sediment series). Standing-water lake gauges (Seepegel, 59 stations in eHYD's surface-water layer on lakes such as Bodensee, Neusiedler See, and Attersee), subsurface spring gauges (Quellen), groundwater wells, and precipitation or evaporation stations are excluded. Validated daily suspended sediment load (Schwebstoff-Tagesfracht) and daily bedload transport (Geschiebe-Tagesfracht) published at a subset of river gauges are also outside RivRetrieve's current quantity scope.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
eHYD publishes river observations through two separate streams:

  1. Validated historical archive (Geprüfte Daten): Quality-checked CSV series reviewed for Austria's Hydrographic Yearbook (Hydrographisches Jahrbuch).
  2. Operational telemetry (Pegel Aktuell): Unchecked near-real-time sub-hourly telemetry (variant="data") and current-year daily comparison series (variant="current_value") published at telemetered gauges.

Validated historical archive (Geprüfte Daten):

Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge owf_abfl_tagesmittel (Q-Tagesmittel) Daily Mean m³/s m³/s discharge owf_abfl_monatsminima (Q-Monatsminima) Monthly Minimum m³/s m³/s discharge owf_abfl_monatsmaxima (Q-Monatsmaxima) Monthly Maximum m³/s m³/s stage owf_wasserst_tagesmittel (W-Tagesmittel) Daily Mean cm m stage owf_wasserst_monatsminima (W-Monatsminima) Monthly (Unknown at 207340) Minimum cm m stage owf_wasserst_monatsmaxima (W-Monatsmaxima) Monthly Maximum cm m temperature owf_wassertemp_monatsmittel (WT-Monatsmittel) Monthly Mean °C °C

Operational telemetry (Pegel Aktuell):

Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge data (sub-hourly telemetry) Unknown Unknown m³/s m³/s stage data (sub-hourly telemetry) Unknown Unknown cm, m ü.A m discharge current_value (current-year daily) Daily Unknown m³/s m³/s stage current_value (current-year daily) Daily Unknown cm, m ü.A m

A station may publish only a subset of these eleven series. Federal eHYD publishes validated river water temperature only as monthly means (owf_wassertemp_monatsmittel); daily and near-real-time river water temperature are not published on this federal service.

In the validated archive, monthly minimum and maximum series report the lowest or highest instantaneous measurement recorded within each calendar month, stamped with its exact occurrence date and time, rather than the lowest or highest daily mean.

RivRetrieve keeps validated archive series and operational telemetry strictly separate. It does not append unchecked telemetry onto validated yearbook records or calculate daily means from sub-hourly readings. Inspect all candidate series and station metadata at a gauge offline before fetching:

all_discharge = rr.find(provider="at_ehyd", station="209486", quantity="discharge")
candidates = rr.series(all_discharge)
metadata = rr.metadata(all_discharge)

Filtering with frequency="daily" and statistic="mean" selects only the validated daily-mean archive series (owf_abfl_tagesmittel) because the current-year daily comparison series (variant="current_value") has no established statistic and the sub-hourly telemetry series (variant="data") has no established frequency or statistic. Select either operational telemetry stream directly with variant:

  • Sub-hourly telemetry (Pegel Aktuell): rr.pick(all_discharge, variant="data") (or rr.pick(all_discharge, time_zone="UTC+01:00"))
  • Current-year daily comparison (Pegel Aktuell): rr.pick(all_discharge, variant="current_value")

You can also pass a specific series_id from candidates to rr.pick(...) when targeting an individual series row.

In sub-hourly telemetry (Pegel Aktuell, variant="data") responses, RivRetrieve reads only the data observation series and omits static warning-level lines (Niedrigwasser, Mittelwasser, and Hochwasser thresholds). In current-year daily comparison (Pegel Aktuell, variant="current_value") responses, RivRetrieve reads only the current calendar year's current_value series; it omits the prior-year overlay (last_year_value, which is aligned onto the current year's 365- or 366-day axis without its own calendar dates) and the 30-year climatological summary curves (min_data, max_data, mit_data, p5_data, p95_data).

docs.title: Stage references and moving gauge zeros
docs.text:
River stage (Wasserstand) in both Geprüfte Daten and Pegel Aktuell is published in centimetres relative to the station's local gauge zero (Pegelnullpunkt). RivRetrieve multiplies cm values by 0.01 to return metres (m), keeps "cm" in source_unit, and sets vertical_reference="gauge_zero" on the series. Genuine water levels below gauge zero remain negative (for example down to -2.27 m at Danube station 207068, Linz), and published negative values in water-temperature exports (down to -2.8 °C in owf_wassertemp_monatsmittel at 200352, Unterhochsteg) are likewise preserved without clamping.

Use care when interpreting multi-year stage records or comparing water levels across periods. At most Austrian river gauges (543 of 739 historical river gauges in the packaged snapshot, 537 with more than one distinct height), the local gauge zero has been reset or resurveyed over time. eHYD's station master sheets (Stammdaten) and stage CSV preambles list dated Pegelnullpunkt heights in metres above the Adriatic datum (m ü.A., Meter über Adria), without stating whether historical stage observations prior to a reset were adjusted to the latest datum or left relative to the datum active at the time of measurement.

Because no single scalar elevation applies across a station's full history, the elevation_* columns are null in rr.metadata(selection) (state="no_metadata" in rr.metadata(selection, view="source")) and vertical_datum remains unknown on stage series. Do not add a single Pegelnullpunkt height to a long stage record without checking the station's dated datum table on eHYD. Where an eHYD stage response declares m ü.A or m ü.A. (Meter über Adria, water-surface elevation above sea level), RivRetrieve returns metres (m) without scaling, with vertical_reference="above_sea_level" and vertical_datum unknown; all river stage series in the packaged snapshot currently publish cm above gauge zero.

Station metadata exposes station names (name from the historical registry and messstelle from Pegel Aktuell), water-body names (gewaesser and gewasser), and orographic catchment area (orogr.Einzugsgebiet [km²] with unit km² for gauges in the historical registry). When name and messstelle spell a gauge's name differently (51 overlapping gauges), summary station_name is null and both spellings remain visible in rr.metadata(selection, view="source"). Catchment areas retain eHYD's German decimal comma as JSON text, such as '"55,3"' at station 209486; see Station metadata for decoding details.

docs.title: Archive vintage and recent coverage
docs.text:
The three series streams cover separate periods and leave an unpublished gap between the latest yearbook and the current calendar year:

  • Validated historical archive (Geprüfte Daten): Covers multi-decade histories up to the close of the latest published Hydrographic Yearbook. In the catalogue snapshot (2026-10-31) and live checks on 2026-11-03, validated river exports end at 2023-12-31 (marked by a closing boundary at 2024-01-01 00:00). Start years vary widely by gauge and quantity, and decommissioned gauges end earlier.
  • Current-year daily comparison (Pegel Aktuell, variant="current_value"): Covers only the current calendar year (2026 during 2026) up to the latest reported day. Trailing null padding for future dates later in the year is trimmed. The service ignores query parameters requesting earlier calendar years.
  • Near-real-time sub-hourly telemetry (Pegel Aktuell, variant="data"): Covers a rolling window of roughly seven to eight days at variable sub-hourly intervals (commonly 5, 10, 15, or 30 minutes, sometimes varying within a single week). Older readings age out as new telemetry arrives. Local caching (cache="reuse") accumulates readings already fetched across repeated runs, while readings that left the rolling window before being fetched cannot be recovered from this service.

Because the validated archive ends at the latest published yearbook (2023) and the current-year daily comparison stream (variant="current_value") serves only the current calendar year, intermediate post-yearbook years (such as 2024 and 2025 before their yearbook release) are not yet available through federal ehyd.gv.at downloads. A validated archive request for dates after 2023-12-31 returns no rows for those unpublished years because the yearbook export has not yet reached them, rather than because no river measurements were taken.

docs.title: Time and data status
docs.text:
Time-zone handling differs between sub-hourly telemetry and the daily or monthly series:

  • Sub-hourly telemetry (Pegel Aktuell, variant="data"): eHYD documents these timestamps as fixed Central European Time (Mitteleuropäische Zeit, MEZ, UTC+01:00 throughout the year without daylight-saving transitions). rr.fetch preserves the published MEZ wall-clock timestamps with time_zone="+01:00" (time_zone="UTC+01:00" in rr.series(...)), and rr.to_utc(result) shifts them to UTC (time_zone="+00:00"). Whether each sub-hourly value represents an instantaneous reading or a short interval average is not established.
  • Validated archive (Geprüfte Daten) and current-year daily comparison (Pegel Aktuell, variant="current_value"): Neither format states an explicit UTC offset in its machine-readable header or payload. Although BMLUK's Pegelordnung 2014 recommends MEZ (UTC+01:00), it also notes historical SOZ/MEZ summer-time practices, and older epochs in validated archive CSV files contain daily timestamps at 07:00 or 01:00 before shifting to 00:00 (at historical manual staff gauges, Lattenpegel, a scheduled morning reading counted as the daily value). RivRetrieve therefore keeps time_zone="unknown" and leaves day_definition unknown on both streams; rr.to_utc() refuses unknown time zones rather than assuming UTC+01:00 across all historical years.

On validated interval-mean archive series (owf_abfl_tagesmittel, owf_wasserst_tagesmittel, and owf_wassertemp_monatsmittel), each timestamp marks the start of its validity interval (timestamp_anchor="start"), in accordance with the CSV preamble rule ("Der Intervallwert gilt bis zum nächsten Zeitpunkt mit einem Wert oder Lücke"). At Danube station 207340 (Wilhering), the W-Monatsminima CSV file declares and contains daily (T,1) stage minima rather than monthly minima; RivRetrieve withholds frequency="monthly" on that station's owf_wasserst_monatsminima series so monthly filters do not return daily rows.

eHYD labels its historical CSV downloads Geprüfte Daten (checked data) and displays "ungeprüfte Rohdaten!" (unchecked raw data) on Pegel Aktuell exports, noting that live telemetry can contain sensor faults, ice or weed effects, backwater, or transmission gaps. Neither stream carries per-observation quality flags. RivRetrieve attaches the verbatim stream label in the series-grain annotation schema at_ehyd.series (scope="series", field data_quality of type String) without making a quality judgement of its own. Use rr.annotations(result) to inspect attached metadata and rr.series(result, annotations=True) to join data_quality to the series table; see Usage.

Keep missing-data representations distinct when inspecting results:

  • In validated archive (Geprüfte Daten) CSV files, missing spans are encoded as timestamped Lücke (gap) transition lines rather than one null row per missing day, and interval files end with a closing Lücke boundary line at the end of the export window. RivRetrieve omits Lücke lines without fabricating rows, suppresses the closing-boundary marker, and records an informational source.gap_marker issue in result.issues when interior gaps occur.
  • In Pegel Aktuell telemetry responses (variant="data" and variant="current_value"), interior missing entries published as null remain rows with value=null.
  • When a Pegel Aktuell gauge is currently offline and returns an empty response, rr.fetch returns no rows (and emits a source.inventory_unresolved warning in result.issues when that telemetry series was requested explicitly). Empty or malformed validated archive files report an error or warning in result.issues; check issues before interpreting an empty result.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
Official INSPIRE Austria metadata records for the hydrographic surface-water station network and the current hydrographic measurement service state that the data are licensed for private and commercial reuse free of charge under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), with mandatory source attribution:

Datenquelle: ehyd.gv.at

In German, the INSPIRE attribution clause requires "Datenquelle: ehyd.gv.at", wobei "ehyd.gv.at" als Link auf https://ehyd.gv.at auszuführen ist (linking ehyd.gv.at to https://ehyd.gv.at). Both rr.describe("at_ehyd") and result.provenance expose license="CC BY 4.0" and citation="Datenquelle: ehyd.gv.at". For scientific traceability, also record the station HZB number, product, requested period, and retrieval date.

The eHYD portal notes that data are published pursuant to § 55o (2) Wasserrechtsgesetz and § 4 (1)(2) Umweltinformationsgesetz without warranty for completeness, continuity, or accuracy, and prohibits automated extraction outside content expressly offered for download (both per-station Geprüfte Daten CSV files and Pegel Aktuell chart CSV exports are offered for download on the portal). An older 2022 general user guide (page 14) also contains an own-use and no-paid-resale statement alongside the CC BY 4.0 INSPIRE licence declarations. RivRetrieve paces live requests politely (at most one request per second) and caches downloaded archive series locally when cache="reuse" is passed.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Publisher documents and metadata checked on 2026-10-31 and verified reachable on 2026-11-03:

  • eHYD portal (ehyd.gv.at): national hydrographic map, station downloads, Pegel Aktuell telemetry charts, and portal legal notices.
  • BMLUK: eHYD Allgemein (general user guide, PDF): HZB numbering, monitoring domains, Stammdaten sheets, CSV exports, and usage notes.
  • BMLUK: Aktuelle Daten in eHYD (current telemetry guide, PDF): Pegel Aktuell transfer intervals and unchecked raw-telemetry caveats.
  • BMLUK: Pegelordnung 2014 (PDF): gauge-zero (Pegelnullpunkt) definitions, time-zone recommendations (MEZ), daily interval means, and monthly instantaneous extrema.
  • LFRZ OGC API Features (i000501): WGS84 (EPSG:4326) station collections for messstellen_owf and pegel_aktuell.
  • INSPIRE Austria metadata: hydrographic station network and Pegel Aktuell service: CC BY 4.0 licensing and mandatory Datenquelle: ehyd.gv.at attribution.

The station counts describe the packaged catalogue snapshot (2026-10-31). The example observations were retrieved on 2026-11-03. This live example does not establish continuous coverage.

docs.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina: AVP Sava
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider ba_fhmzbih Country Bosnia and Herzegovina Published by Agencija za vodno područje rijeke Save (AVP Sava), the Sava River Watershed Agency, Sarajevo Read from AVP Sava's hydrological monitoring site (vodostaji.voda.ba) Quantities Discharge, stage and water temperature Stations in the catalogue 60. Availability depends on quantity and period Station metadata Drainage area. See Fields by provider Credentials None History available Rolling yearly workbooks; records can be shorter and have gaps Terms Data are informational, not official. See Terms and citation Agency documentation Hydrological monitoring, Impressum

RivRetrieve reads the workbooks published by AVP Sava. Retrieve discharge for three days at station 2310, HS Ključ on the Sana:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="ba_fhmzbih",
    station="2310",
    quantity="discharge",
)

result = rr.fetch(
    selection,
    start="2026-09-01",
    end="2026-09-03T23:59:59",
    cache="bypass",
)

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print([(issue.severity, issue.code) for issue in result.issues])

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2026-09-01T01:00:00.000000,unknown,,m3/s
2026-09-01T02:00:00.000000,unknown,3.9330000000000003,m3/s
2026-09-01T03:00:00.000000,unknown,3.943,m3/s
69
[('info', 'provenance.license_not_established'), ('info', 'provenance.citation_not_established')]

The request returned 69 rows in m³/s, including six null values. The preview shows the first three rows. The empty value at 01:00 is a published blank, returned as value=null. There is no observation row for midnight on September 1. These are different forms of missing data. The explicit end time includes observations through the end of September 3; it does not request a daily mean.

The two informational issues mean that RivRetrieve has not established a licence or citation for this provider. They do not report a failed observation request. Successful retrieval does not establish measurement quality. Check issues before interpreting the result.

cache="bypass" requests the source rather than a local observation cache. This output was checked live on 2026-09-28. The workbooks roll forward, so this fixed period will eventually fall outside their available history. Published values can also change. Choose a recent period when running the example later. See Usage for general selection and result handling.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
Bosnia and Herzegovina's rivers drain towards the Black Sea through the Sava and Danube, or towards the Adriatic Sea. AVP Sava's area of responsibility is the Black Sea drainage area within the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, one of the country's two entities. This is not nationwide coverage.

The agency organises hydrological monitoring and collects and distributes water resource data. Its water information system collects, processes and displays observations from automatic stations. These institutional responsibilities do not establish the owner or measurement operator of every station in RivRetrieve's catalogue.

The Federal Hydrometeorological Institute (FHMZBiH) is a separate institution. Its hydrology page directs readers to AVP Sava and the Adriatic Sea Watershed Agency for observations collected by their water information systems.

The provider identifier is ba_fhmzbih, but the publisher of the workbooks RivRetrieve reads is AVP Sava. The identifier does not mean that RivRetrieve provides a national inventory or all data held by Bosnia and Herzegovina's hydrometeorological services. Broader geographical coverage and an AVP Sava provider name with compatibility for ba_fhmzbih are on the roadmap (#406).

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge Proticaj Unknown Unknown m³/s m³/s stage Vodostaj Unknown Unknown cm m temperature Temperatura vode Unknown Unknown °C °C

RivRetrieve converts stage from centimetres to metres. Discharge and water temperature need no unit conversion. Stage is water level; its vertical reference or datum has not been established.

The catalogue contains 60 stations. Its recorded availability checks found numerical discharge and stage values at all 60, and water temperature at 12. Temperature availability remains unknown at the other 48, which are still selectable. A station being listed does not guarantee that it has data for every quantity or requested period.

The source does not establish whether these values are instantaneous readings or averages. RivRetrieve leaves frequency, statistic and temporal support unknown. Approximately hourly spacing does not establish an hourly mean. Select by quantity without assuming a frequency or statistic.

docs.title: How far back, and how recent
docs.text:
RivRetrieve reads the source's yearly workbooks. These offer a rolling window, not a permanent archive. On 2026-09-28, the discharge and stage workbooks at HS Ključ held timestamps from September 29, 2025 to September 28, 2026, with gaps. A yearly workbook need not contain a full year of readings or recent values: the water-temperature workbook at HS Ilidža (4110) held only September 29 to November 30, 2025.

A request can return only observations still present in the workbook. It cannot recover older observations that have rolled out of the source file. Contact the agency about longer records; this interface does not establish their availability. Access to archival records is on the roadmap (#407).

docs.title: Time and data status
docs.text:
The workbooks publish timestamps without an established time zone. RivRetrieve returns these labels in time, paired with time_zone="unknown". Do not infer UTC or local civil time from the station's location. The period represented by each value is also unknown.

The site's Impressum states:

Svi podaci koji se prikazuju i koji se dobiju kao rezultat pretrage su informativnog karaktera i ne mogu služiti kao zvanični podaci.

In English, unofficially: all data displayed, and all data obtained as search results, are for information only and cannot serve as official data.

The workbooks read here contain timestamps and values without observation-level quality or approval flags. RivRetrieve makes no quality judgement of its own. A published blank remains a row with value=null. An absent observation supplies no row. A failed request remains an issue alongside any successful records.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
The portal's Impressum does not specify a reuse licence or a citation format. AVP Sava's main website carries an “All rights reserved” copyright notice. These pages do not establish data-specific reuse permission. Check reuse conditions with the agency before redistributing the data.

For traceability, name AVP Sava and retain the station, quantity, requested period and access date. This is practical guidance, not a publisher citation template.

docs.title: Brazil: ANA
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider br_ana Country Brazil Published by Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA) Quantities Discharge and stage Stations in the catalogue 17,914. Availability depends on quantity, source selection and period Station metadata Station name, water-body name, drainage area and elevation. See Fields by provider Credentials Required for retrieval: ANA_IDENTIFICADOR, ANA_SENHA Terms stated by ANA Open data made freely available; see Terms and citation Agency documentation HidroWebService, Hidroweb

With credentials configured, retrieve three days of published daily mean discharge at station 15400000, choosing ANA's consistido consistency level:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="br_ana",
    station="15400000",
    quantity="discharge",
    frequency="daily",
    statistic="mean",
)
consistido = rr.pick(selection, variant="consistido")

result = rr.fetch(
    consistido, start="2020-01-10", end="2020-01-12", cache="bypass"
)

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit")
print(preview.write_csv(), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print(sorted({(issue.severity, issue.code) for issue in result.issues}))
print(
    result.to_polars(annotations=True)
    .select("Vazao_Status", "Metodo_Obtencao_Vazoes")
    .rows()
)

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2020-01-10T00:00:00.000000,unknown,31687.982,m3/s
2020-01-11T00:00:00.000000,unknown,31789.021,m3/s
2020-01-12T00:00:00.000000,unknown,31553.52,m3/s
3
[('info', 'provenance.citation_not_established')]
[('1', '1'), ('1', '1'), ('1', '1')]

The three rows contain source-published daily means in m³/s, and each row carries Vazao_Status='1' and Metodo_Obtencao_Vazoes='1' from br_ana.daily_vazao. Both endpoint dates are included. RivRetrieve does not calculate these means. cache="bypass" requests the source rather than cached observations. The citation issue means that RivRetrieve has not established a standard citation, rather than indicating a failed observation request.

The time zone is unknown; midnight labels do not establish the hours covered by each mean. Source values can change, so a later request may not reproduce this output exactly. Run the following examples in the same session. See Usage for general selection and result handling.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
ANA, Brazil's national water and sanitation agency, coordinates the Rede Hidrometeorológica Nacional (unofficially, National Hydrometeorological Network). Public and private organisations operate its stations under ANA's supervision. Specialist staff and field observers collect the measurements; ANA standardises measurement procedures and equipment.

ANA makes hydrological records available through Hidroweb. RivRetrieve reads its programming interface, HidroWebService. ANA's role as publisher does not identify the original producer of every measurement.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
Catalogue selection works without credentials. Observation retrieval requires an ANA identifier and password, issued on request.

ANA's Solicite Acesso API page asks for an email to telemetria@ana.gov.br, with the subject "Solicitação de acesso à API", a short explanation of the intended use, and:

  • the name of the user or institution;
  • a CPF or CNPJ (Brazilian personal or company tax number), used as the username;
  • an email address to receive the password.

The page does not say what applicants without a CPF or CNPJ should provide. ANA reviews the request and may ask for more information. Use the issued Identificador and Senha (unofficially, identifier and password). The identifier is not the account email address.

Set ANA_IDENTIFICADOR and ANA_SENHA in the process environment or in a private .env file in the directory from which Python runs. Process variables take precedence, including blank values. Keep credentials out of code, version control, logs and shared files. See credential setup for details.

rr.providers() reports ready when both credentials are present locally. It does not authenticate with ANA or prove that the credentials are accepted.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
ANA publishes two kinds of series. Daily series are source-published daily means, selected by consistency level, bruto or consistido (see Daily consistency levels). Telemetry series are ANA's adopted discharge and stage values, Vazao_Adotada and Cota_Adotada, each labelled with its measurement time.

Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge bruto, consistido Daily Mean m³/s m³/s stage bruto, consistido Daily Mean cm m discharge Vazao_Adotada Unknown Unknown m³/s m³/s stage Cota_Adotada Unknown Unknown cm m

RivRetrieve divides stage values by 100 to convert centimetres to metres. Discharge is already in m³/s. Water temperature is currently not supported.

ANA's API manual documents the telemetry fields' names, units and measurement timestamps, but not how often they are sampled or whether each value is a spot reading or an average. RivRetrieve therefore leaves frequency and statistic unknown for these fields. Filters match only known values, so adding frequency="daily" or statistic="instantaneous" to rr.find() excludes the telemetry series. Select them by variant instead:

telemetry = rr.pick(
    rr.find(provider="br_ana", station="15400000", quantity="discharge"),
    variant="Vazao_Adotada",
)

print(rr.series(telemetry).select("variant", "frequency", "statistic").rows())

Output:

[('Vazao_Adotada', None, None)]

This selects a catalogue candidate; it does not retrieve telemetry observations. For every station, the catalogue lists the six series in the table above. A station being listed does not guarantee observations for every quantity, source selection or requested period. The successful daily example establishes availability only for that station, selection and period, not continuous history or national coverage.

docs.title: Daily consistency levels: bruto and consistido
docs.text:
ANA identifies daily records by NivelConsistencia: level 1, bruto, and level 2, consistido. Unofficially, these mean raw and consistency-checked values. They are source categories, not a quality ranking assigned by RivRetrieve.

Inspect the daily discharge candidates selected above:

print(
    rr.series(selection)
    .select("station_id", "variant", "frequency", "statistic")
    .rows()
)

Output:

[('15400000', 'bruto', 'daily', 'mean'), ('15400000', 'consistido', 'daily', 'mean')]

rr.pick(selection, variant="bruto") selects the other level. Fetching selection without narrowing it requests both and keeps their source identities separate:

both_result = rr.fetch(
    selection, start="2020-01-10", end="2020-01-12", cache="bypass"
)

print(rr.series(both_result).select("variant").rows())
print(both_result.data.height, both_result.data["series_id"].n_unique())
print(sorted({(issue.severity, issue.code) for issue in both_result.issues}))

Output:

[('bruto',), ('consistido',)]
3 1
[('info', 'provenance.citation_not_established'), ('warning', 'source.unresolved_inventory')]

The second line shows 3 rows from 1 series: the response supplied three consistido observations and no bruto observations. Both identities remain in the series inspection table, but only one has returned rows. source.unresolved_inventory means the response did not establish availability for the requested bruto level. The default issue policy also emits a Python warning with that explanation. This is a partial result, not evidence that bruto is absent from the station's entire history.

The same station and date can have one value per consistency level, so keep series_id when comparing records. RivRetrieve neither averages the consistency levels nor selects a preferred one. An explicit choice does not fall back to the other level. If ANA's response does not publish the requested level, its availability remains unresolved, and an issue reports that limitation rather than substituting observations.

docs.title: Time and source status
docs.text:
Returned time contains source clock labels accompanied by time_zone="unknown". Read those columns together. RivRetrieve has not established the source time zone or the interval covered by a daily mean. It does not infer either from station location or the midnight representation of a daily date.

ANA also supplies verbatim status and method fields for observations. RivRetrieve attaches them in four observation-grain annotation schemas (String) without interpreting them as a quality ranking:

  • br_ana.daily_cotas: Cota_Status and Tipo_Medicao_Cotas.
  • br_ana.daily_vazao: Vazao_Status and Metodo_Obtencao_Vazoes.
  • br_ana.telemetry_cota: Cota_Adotada_Status.
  • br_ana.telemetry_vazao: Vazao_Adotada_Status.

These attached fields are distinct from the selectable daily consistency levels. Use rr.annotations(result) to inspect attached schemas and result.to_polars(annotations=True) or result.to_pandas(annotations=True) to project them onto returned rows; see Usage.

A blank or null daily value remains a row with value=null. An absent source record remains absent, and a failed request is reported separately in issues. RivRetrieve does not fill gaps. Check issues before interpreting empty or partial results.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
ANA's open data page states:

Os dados abertos são disponibilizados livremente para a utilização de toda a sociedade, sem restrição de licenças, patentes ou mecanismos de controle.

In English, unofficially: open data are made freely available for use by all of society, without restriction of licences, patents or control mechanisms.

This is ANA's institutional open-data statement. No citation format for these observations was found in the sources checked for this page, and RivRetrieve reports the missing citation as an informational notice. When citing the data, we suggest naming ANA and Hidroweb as the source, along with the stations, the series used (bruto, consistido or telemetry) and the date of retrieval.

docs.title: Canada: Environment and Climate Change Canada
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider ca_eccc Country Canada Published by Water Survey of Canada, Environment and Climate Change Canada Quantities Daily mean discharge and stage Stations in the catalogue 8,057. Availability depends on quantity and period Station metadata Station name and drainage area. See Fields by provider Credentials None Access Explicit national HYDAT download, then local retrieval Terms The official HYDAT dataset record lists the Open Government Licence – Canada; see Terms and citation Agency documentation Water Office, National water data archive: HYDAT

First prepare the national archive. This transfers and compiles the whole dataset, not just the station used below. Allow time and disk space for that operation; see Downloading the archive.

import rivretrieve as rr

rr.download("ca_eccc")

Then retrieve one week of published daily mean discharge at station 05OG008:

selection = rr.find(
    provider="ca_eccc",
    station="05OG008",
    quantity="discharge",
    frequency="daily",
    statistic="mean",
)

result = rr.fetch(
    selection, start="1991-03-01", end="1991-03-07", cache="bypass"
)

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(float_precision=3), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print(result.issues)

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
1991-03-01T00:00:00.000000,unknown,0.090,m3/s
1991-03-02T00:00:00.000000,unknown,0.090,m3/s
1991-03-03T00:00:00.000000,unknown,0.090,m3/s
7
()

The request returned seven daily means in m³/s and no retrieval issues (the empty tuple ()). The preview shows three values rounded to three decimal places. Both endpoint dates are included. RivRetrieve reads the published means; it does not calculate them from more frequent observations. An empty issue tuple does not establish the quality of the values.

For this bulk provider, cache="bypass" still reads the compiled local archive. This example was checked using the July 17, 2026 HYDAT release. Historical values may change in later releases. Run the snippets in order in the same Python session. See Usage for general selection and result handling.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
The Water Survey of Canada (WSC), within Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), collects, interprets and publishes standardized water-quantity data. The national hydrometric program operates through federal, provincial and territorial partnerships and agreements with other organisations. WSC operates stations for most provinces and territories; Quebec operates its own network.

WSC compiles the historical records in HYDAT and publishes near-real-time data through the Water Office and other services. RivRetrieve reads the HYDAT SQLite archive, not the near-real-time service. ECCC describes HYDAT updates as quarterly. An archive edition date does not tell you the latest observation date at each station or establish a fixed publication delay.

docs.title: Downloading the archive
docs.text:
rr.download("ca_eccc") explicitly downloads and compiles the national archive. RivRetrieve never starts this transfer during fetch. Without a compiled store, retrieval returns an empty result with a bulk.store_missing warning and an instruction to run download.

The July 17, 2026 compressed SQLite archive was listed as approximately 266 MB by the publisher. Compilation also needs space for the extracted database and working files. The verified compiled store occupied about 383 MB; that is not its peak working-space requirement. The fresh download and compilation took about an hour on the verification machine. Size and duration vary by edition and computer. RivRetrieve checks its configured free-space requirement before starting; allow additional working space rather than treating the ZIP size as the disk requirement.

Choose a cache location with RIVRETRIEVE_CACHE_DIR before preparing the archive; see cache configuration. After preparation, inspect the local copy without downloading it again:

status = rr.cache_status("ca_eccc")

print(status.presence.value)
print(status.source_vintage)

Output for the verified copy:

present
2026-07-17

The same compiled copy serves later requests for other stations and periods. Both cache="bypass" and cache="reuse" read it locally. cache="refresh" is refused: run rr.download("ca_eccc") explicitly to replace the store with the latest available edition. Retrieval does not check for a newer archive.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge FLOW in DLY_FLOWS Daily Mean m³/s m³/s stage LEVEL in DLY_LEVELS Daily Mean m m

Use frequency="daily" and statistic="mean" for either quantity. Stage is water level, not water depth or automatically an elevation above sea level. RivRetrieve has not established a vertical reference for these series. Other HYDAT contents, including sediment and extremes, are outside this provider's supported quantities and statistics.

A station being listed does not guarantee data for each quantity or requested period. The packaged catalogue does not establish station record dates or per-quantity availability. The example verifies only its station, quantity and week, not continuous history or national coverage.

docs.title: Time and data status
docs.text:
Daily calendar dates appear at midnight with time_zone="unknown". Read time and time_zone together. RivRetrieve has not established the time zone or the interval bounds for these historical daily series. The midnight label does not make them UTC. ECCC's FAQ describes daily means using observations between 00:00 and 24:00; this does not establish a zone for every historical record returned here.

ECCC describes review and finalization before records enter its national historical database. Values can still carry source symbols, including B for ice conditions and E for estimates, and can be revised. RivRetrieve preserves HYDAT daily qualifier symbols and water-level recording precision codes as attached observation annotations without adding quality columns to result.data, ranking symbols, or filtering observations:

  • ca_eccc.dly_flows: symbol (String).
  • ca_eccc.dly_levels: symbol (String) and precision_code (Int64).

HYDAT defines daily qualifier codes in DATA_SYMBOLS (A partial day, B ice conditions, D dry, E estimated, and S sample collected this day). Some historical months also store single-space strings " " in symbol cells. RivRetrieve preserves " " verbatim, distinct from null when no symbol cell value was published.

For daily water levels, precision_code preserves PRECISION_CODES (8 for metres recorded to millimetres, 9 for metres recorded to centimetres). Because HYDAT records PRECISION_CODE per monthly table row and a station's precision code can change mid-year, RivRetrieve attaches each month's code to every daily row of that month.

Inspect the annotation field catalogue on result and project symbol onto the March 1991 discharge rows fetched above:

print(rr.annotations(result).select("schema", "name", "dtype").rows())

annotated = result.to_polars(annotations=True)
symbol_preview = annotated.select("time", "value", "symbol").head(3)
print(symbol_preview.write_csv(float_precision=3), end="")

Output:

[('ca_eccc.dly_flows', 'symbol', 'String')]
time,value,symbol
1991-03-01T00:00:00.000000,0.090,B
1991-03-02T00:00:00.000000,0.090,B
1991-03-03T00:00:00.000000,0.090,B

Notice that all three shown March 1991 discharge means carry symbol B for ice conditions even though result.issues was empty. Pass annotations="symbol" to result.to_polars(...) or result.to_pandas(...) when you want specific annotation columns, or call rr.annotations(result, schema="ca_eccc.dly_flows") for the native schema table. Monthly summary fields (FULL_MONTH, NO_DAYS, MONTHLY_MEAN, MONTHLY_TOTAL, FIRST_DAY_MIN, MIN, FIRST_DAY_MAX, MAX) remain in optional store-excerpt receipts; a store excerpt is not the original national ZIP archive.

A published null daily cell remains a row with value=null. An absent monthly source record supplies no daily rows. A missing store or failed request is reported separately; an empty result alone does not distinguish those cases. Check issues before interpreting gaps or empty results.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
The official Historical Hydrometric Data dataset record links the HYDAT SQL download and lists the Open Government Licence – Canada. It permits reuse, including commercial use, subject to its conditions, and requires source attribution and, where possible, a licence link. Where no specific attribution is supplied, its wording is:

Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada.

ECCC also publishes a separate Data Services End-use Licence, which its hydrometric data-server documentation cites and RivRetrieve records as a provenance source. Its attribution provisions include third-party originators. These are distinct publisher licence statements. Check the linked terms that apply to the source and intended use.

The Water Office FAQ provides separate citations for its websites and for HYDAT.mdb. That MDB-specific wording is not a prescribed SQLite citation. For the SQLite archive, a practical reference should identify ECCC/WSC, HYDAT, the actual SQLite edition, source URL and access date. This is suggested documentation of the source, not an official citation template. The Water Office's conditions for information on its website should not be assumed to define the archive's reuse terms.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Publisher pages checked on 2026-09-22:

  • WSC overview, Water Office FAQ: responsibilities, daily means and symbols, citation guidance.
  • HYDAT archive, download directory, HYDAT definition: archive contents, table definitions, publication and edition.
  • Historical Hydrometric Data record, Open Government Licence, ECCC Data Services End-use Licence: terms and attribution.

docs.title: Switzerland: FOEN
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider ch_foen Country Switzerland Published by Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU) and partner measurement networks Read from Official BAFU GraphQL API Quantities Discharge, stage, water temperature Stations in the catalogue 1,341. Availability depends on station, quantity, product and period Station metadata Station name, water-body name, drainage area and elevation. See Fields by provider Credentials None Terms Commercial and non-commercial use permitted; source attribution required Agency documentation Water observations

Retrieve published daily mean discharge at station 2018, selecting the archive variant TagMittel:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="ch_foen", station="2018", quantity="discharge",
    frequency="daily", statistic="mean",
)
daily = rr.pick(selection, variant="TagMittel")
result = rr.fetch(daily, start="2024-01-01", end="2024-01-07", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(float_precision=3), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print([(issue.severity, issue.code) for issue in result.issues])

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2023-12-31T23:00:00.000000,+00:00,113.624,m3/s
2024-01-01T23:00:00.000000,+00:00,107.088,m3/s
2024-01-02T23:00:00.000000,+00:00,114.261,m3/s
7
[('info', 'provenance.citation_not_established')]

The request returned seven daily means in m³/s. The preview shows the first three, rounded to three decimal places. Each day begins at midnight in fixed UTC+1, so 1 January's mean is labelled 31 December at 23:00 UTC. Bare dates select the whole first and last aggregate day. RivRetrieve preserves these UTC labels rather than moving them to midnight UTC or applying summer time.

The informational issue provenance.citation_not_established means the packaged provider catalogue has no configured citation. It does not mean retrieval failed or that attribution is optional. Use the attribution in Terms. cache="bypass" requests the source rather than a local cache. Values can change; a later retrieval need not reproduce this output exactly. See Usage for selection options and working with returned data.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
The Federal Office for the Environment runs Switzerland's national hydrological monitoring network. BAFU is its German abbreviation, from Bundesamt für Umwelt; FOEN is its English abbreviation. The official data platform brings together BAFU and partner measurement networks. Its publisher name does not mean that BAFU independently measured every observation.

No API key or account is required to retrieve observations. RivRetrieve searches the station and product catalogue included with the package without contacting BAFU. Fetching observations then requests data from the official API.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Choose an archive product according to the period and statistic needed for the analysis. For example, the daily mean describes a day as a whole, while the daily maximum describes its highest short-term measurement. The available product types are listed below for discharge (discharge), water level (stage) and water temperature (temperature). A particular station may supply only some of these products.

Frequency filter Statistic filter Product 10min mean Ten-minute mean hourly mean Hourly mean daily mean, min, max Daily mean, minimum or maximum monthly mean, min, max Monthly mean, minimum or maximum yearly mean, min, max Yearly mean, minimum or maximum

The API also supplies recent raw readings separately from the archive products above. RivRetrieve has not established the exact period represented by each recent reading or its statistic, such as a mean. Its timestamp marks measurement end, but the averaging duration remains unknown; do not treat the reading as an instantaneous measurement. A daily-mean selection therefore excludes these recent readings and selects only products known to represent daily means.

For minimum and maximum products, the aggregate period tells you where to look for the extreme, not how long the underlying measurement lasted. A monthly maximum, for example, is the maximum of short-term measurements within the month, rather than the largest daily mean. The exact measurement duration and the time when that maximum occurred remain unknown.

RivRetrieve retrieves the products BAFU publishes. It does not calculate missing products from other values or combine recent readings with archive aggregates. The public product page's abbreviated list omits some supported monthly and yearly extrema. Availability still varies by station and quantity.

Quantity filter Source units Returned unit discharge m³/s or l/s m³/s (m3/s) stage m or cm, with source reference labels where published m (m) temperature °C °C (degC)

RivRetrieve converts litres per second to cubic metres per second and centimetres to metres. For archive data, RivRetrieve reads the unit supplied with the API response. For recent readings, it uses the unit shown for that parameter on the official station page. The original unit remains visible in source_unit; do not assume archive and recent units are identical. Water-level references need care when comparing records. A label such as “above sea level” tells you what the height refers to, but it does not establish which named height reference system (vertical datum) applies to that series. Although station metadata can identify LN02 for the station altitude, that describes the station's elevation, not necessarily the reference used for its water-level observations.

docs.title: Series selection
docs.text:
A station can publish more than one series for the same quantity and product. The archive distinguishes them by a name in its tsName field, which RivRetrieve returns as variant. At station 2602, for example, both TagMittel and TagMittel_01 are daily-mean series covering overlapping periods. The suffix does not tell you which record is better. RivRetrieve keeps the series separate rather than choosing one automatically or combining their values. Selecting a variant explicitly chooses that series. The recent feed is separate and has no archive tsName.

Inspect the candidates and station metadata before choosing a series:

candidates = rr.series(selection)
metadata = rr.metadata(selection)

candidates describes known series, including their units, frequency and statistic; metadata describes the station. The first example explicitly selects TagMittel. Without a specific variant, RivRetrieve may request data again to look for other source series. Selecting a known variant allows it to reuse cached observations for periods already fetched. See Usage for cache policies.

docs.title: Recent and older values
docs.text:
The catalogue lists 1,341 stations, but it does not list every product available at every station. A station being listed does not guarantee data for every product or period. Conversely, a product missing from a station's catalogue entry may still exist at the source. Station operating dates and the timestamps of a few retrieved values do not establish how far the API record extends.

It remains unclear how far back recent readings can be requested. The API documentation says seven days in one place and twelve hours in another, so RivRetrieve cannot promise either period. A cache can preserve readings already fetched, but it cannot recover readings that disappeared from the source before they were fetched. We are in touch with BAFU and will update this information as soon as these limits are clarified.

When inspecting a result, distinguish a row whose value is null from a timestamp that has no row at all. In the first case the source returned an entry without a value; in the second there is no returned entry. RivRetrieve preserves that difference and does not fill gaps. A failed request is a third case: inspect result.issues rather than treating a retrieval failure as evidence that the source has no data. Even a successful request only shows what was returned for that station, product and period; it does not prove an uninterrupted record.

The separate official Hydrological Data Service for watercourses and lakes offers historical data by order, including data beyond what has been verified through this provider. Orders go directly to that service; RivRetrieve does not place them or use the service when an API request fails. The service's statement about 40 days online refers to a different means of obtaining data and does not resolve the conflicting limits for recent GraphQL readings.

docs.title: Data status
docs.text:
BAFU publishes a release and validation status alongside its observations. RivRetrieve keeps the default observation table in result.data unchanged and preserves those source status fields as observation annotations:

Route group Annotation schema Field Type Archive (10min, hourly, daily, monthly, yearly) ch_foen.archive releaseState String Recent (discharge_recent, stage_recent, water_temperature_recent) ch_foen.recent releaseStatus Int64

Inspect available annotation fields and join them onto the observations fetched at the start of this page:

print(
    rr.annotations(result)
    .select("schema", "name", "dtype", "row_count")
    .write_csv(),
    end="",
)

annotated = result.to_polars(annotations=True).select(
    "time", "value", "unit", "releaseState"
)
print(annotated.head(3).write_csv(float_precision=3), end="")

Output:

schema,name,dtype,row_count
ch_foen.archive,releaseState,String,7
time,value,unit,releaseState
2023-12-31T23:00:00.000000,113.624,m3/s,3
2024-01-01T23:00:00.000000,107.088,m3/s,3
2024-01-02T23:00:00.000000,114.261,m3/s,3

Every daily value in that week carries archive releaseState '3'. Call rr.annotations(result, schema="ch_foen.archive") or rr.annotations(result, schema="ch_foen.recent") to inspect one route schema on its own. Keeping archive and recent tables separate prevents a missing recent or archive column in a combined query from looking like a published null status.

Source status Publisher meaning null or 0 Raw 1 Unreleased / prechecked 2 Released / checked 3 Released / definitive

BAFU explains that a null status has the same meaning as 0, raw. RivRetrieve keeps explicit null, string '0', and integer 0 as published rather than converting one into another. Published observations whose value is null still retain their status annotations.

BAFU's German documentation also writes ersetzt (replaced) beside status 3, without defining which series replaced another. RivRetrieve therefore uses these fields only to report source status: it does not filter observations by status, convert codes into a cross-provider quality score, or rank tsName variants.

Status annotations travel with local cache entries, manual cache="refresh" updates, UTC conversion, subsetting, and exported bundles. See Source annotations for general options, or Receipts when you need the original HTTP response payload.

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
Two time conventions matter when interpreting archive values: the clock used to display the timestamp and the calendar used to define the aggregate period. RivRetrieve returns timestamps in UTC, indicated by time_zone="+00:00". Read this column together with time, whose datetime values do not themselves carry a time zone.

Ordinary aggregate timestamps identify the start of the represented period. For daily, monthly and yearly products, that period begins at midnight in fixed UTC+1, including summer. Midnight in this calendar is 23:00 UTC on the preceding date, which explains the labels in the retrieval example. February 2024, for instance, runs from 31 January at 23:00 UTC up to, but not including, 29 February at 23:00 UTC. Its January UTC label still represents the February aggregate; changing the label to midnight UTC would change the period it identifies.

Recent timestamps mark measurement end; their spacing does not establish an averaging duration. For station 7008's unusual MonatsMittel_Orbe_flex series, RivRetrieve has not established the period each value represents, its statistic, or whether its timestamp marks the beginning or end of that period. Neither the series name nor the API route establishes daily or monthly values. The series is therefore excluded by filters requiring those known properties.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
The API terms permit commercial and non-commercial use and require attribution containing the author, dataset title and dataset link. The linked open-data terms describe this condition as “Open use. Must provide the source”. These are the platform's terms of use, rather than a CC-BY licence. Attribution is required when using data retrieved through this API.

Suggested attribution:

Bundesamt für Umwelt BAFU, Hydrologische Beobachtungen, https://data.bafu.admin.ch/dataproduct-water-observations

This is a suggested composition of the required fields, not an official template or quotation. An access date is useful but is not one of those three required fields.

The API allows data requests without an API key or account, but it limits how often a client can request data. Its rate limit is 500 requests per client IP within any rolling five-minute window. Requests above that limit are rejected with HTTP 403, so a large retrieval can fail even though access is open. RivRetrieve does not promise to wait and retry that response automatically. The API also documents pagination and result limits.

docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider co_ideam Country Colombia Published by Instituto de Hidrología, Meteorología y Estudios Ambientales (IDEAM) Read from IDEAM Open Data historical S3 archive (datos.ideam.gov.co) Quantities Discharge, stage Stations in the catalogue 1,372 river gauges.
