Retrieve one week of daily mean discharge at station 0011017010, Aguasal on the Andágueda river in Chocó:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="co_ideam",
    station="0011017010",
    quantity="discharge",
    frequency="daily",
    statistic="mean",
)

result = rr.fetch(selection, start="2010-01-01", end="2010-01-07", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print(result.issues)

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2010-01-01T00:00:00.000000,unknown,128.7,m3/s
2010-01-02T00:00:00.000000,unknown,126.3,m3/s
2010-01-03T00:00:00.000000,unknown,162.8,m3/s
7
()

The request returned seven published daily means in m³/s from IDEAM's Q_MEDIA_D historical CSV file. The preview shows the first three days. time_zone is unknown because the exported CSV files carry no UTC offset and reflect a 1992-1993 national clock change; see Time and data status. The empty tuple () means this retrieval reported no transport or structural issues. Attribution and ShareAlike conditions apply when reusing the data; see Terms and citation.

cache="bypass", the default for live rr.fetch calls, requests IDEAM's S3 archive directly without reading or writing a local cache. Passing cache="reuse" stores the downloaded series locally so later historical queries within the cached span reuse the local store without downloading the multi-decade CSV file again. This output was checked live on 2026-11-09. Published values can change when IDEAM revises provisional rating curves. See Usage for selection options and result handling.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
Colombia's Instituto de Hidrología, Meteorología y Estudios Ambientales (IDEAM), a public scientific institute affiliated with the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible), operates the national hydrometeorological monitoring network and publishes historical surface-water series from its AQUARIUS Time-Series database to its Open Data S3 portal (datos.ideam.gov.co). Some stations in the national registry are operated by regional environmental authorities (Corporaciones Autónomas Regionales) or hydropower and water utilities and shared through IDEAM's national catalogue.

No API key or account is required. RivRetrieve searches the packaged station and series catalogue offline; rr.fetch then downloads the corresponding per-station CSV files over HTTPS. Station identifiers are ten-digit zero-padded IDEAM codes, kept as strings such as "0011017010". Include the two leading zeros when selecting by station code, even though station display names often show the eight-digit form in brackets (for example AGUASAL [11017010]).

The packaged co_ideam catalogue retains 1,372 flowing-watercourse gauges that publish at least one river discharge or stage file in IDEAM's S3 historical archive:

  • Excluded non-river and inactive entries: Socrata station-registry rows with no S3 discharge or stage files, meteorological-only stations, and standing-water stage gauges on reservoirs (Embalse) and lagoons (Laguna) without discharge series are excluded. Gauges classified under a hydrological station category that publish river discharge or stream-named stage records are retained.
  • Separation from legacy HIS_* Socrata tables: Colombia's national open data portal (datos.gov.co) also hosts older tabular datasets named HIS_CAUDAL_D, HIS_NIVEL_D, and similar HIS_* views. Those legacy tables stop around 2019 to 2022 and are superseded by IDEAM's daily-regenerated S3 historical CSV archive (s3-estacionesideam), which carries both the earlier multi-decade history and current operational years. RivRetrieve reads only the S3 historical CSV archive and does not query or merge the legacy HIS_* tables.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
IDEAM publishes up to twenty hydrological CSV series per river gauge: ten for discharge (caudal) and ten for water level (nivel):

Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge CAUDAL_H Unknown Unknown m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MEDIA_D Daily Mean m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MX_D Daily Maximum m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MN_D Daily Minimum m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MEDIA_M Monthly Mean m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MX_M Monthly Maximum m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MN_M Monthly Minimum m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MEDIA_A Yearly Mean m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MX_A Yearly Maximum m³/s m³/s discharge Q_MN_A Yearly Minimum m³/s m³/s stage NIVEL_H Unknown Unknown cm m stage NV_MEDIA_D Daily Mean cm m stage NV_MX_D Daily Maximum cm m stage NV_MN_D Daily Minimum cm m stage NV_MEDIA_M Monthly Mean cm m stage NV_MX_M Monthly Maximum cm m stage NV_MN_M Monthly Minimum cm m stage NV_MEDIA_A Yearly Mean cm m stage NV_MX_A Yearly Maximum cm m stage NV_MN_A Yearly Minimum cm m

A station may publish only a subset of these twenty files, and a listed series need not cover the requested period. RivRetrieve reads the aggregated daily, monthly, and yearly series directly as IDEAM publishes them; it does not compute daily, monthly, or yearly summaries from sub-daily readings.

IDEAM's variables.csv dictionary labels CAUDAL_H and NIVEL_H as Horario (hourly) with no statistic code. In practice, those two labels combine hourly telemetry at automatic gauges with twice-daily (06:00 and 18:00) manual staff-gauge readings at conventional gauges, and individual stations switch cadence when upgraded from conventional observation to telemetry. Because one series label spans both observation schedules without declaring whether readings are instantaneous or interval averages, RivRetrieve leaves both frequency and statistic unknown (None) on CAUDAL_H and NIVEL_H.

Filtering by frequency ("daily", "monthly", or "yearly") and statistic ("mean", "max", or "min") selects the corresponding derived series directly. To inspect all available series at a gauge offline or select CAUDAL_H or NIVEL_H explicitly, inspect rr.series(...) and pick by series_id:

import polars as pl

all_discharge = rr.find(provider="co_ideam", station="0011017010", quantity="discharge")
candidates = rr.series(all_discharge)
metadata = rr.metadata(all_discharge)

caudal_h_id = candidates.filter(pl.col("published_id") == "CAUDAL_H")["series_id"].item()
subdaily = rr.pick(all_discharge, series_id=caudal_h_id)

At automatic telemetric gauges, IDEAM derives daily maxima (Q_MX_D, NV_MX_D) and minima (Q_MN_D, NV_MN_D) from intra-hour sensor extremes, which can exceed the highest top-of-hour reading in CAUDAL_H or NIVEL_H on the same date. Because sub-daily averaging and extreme-value conventions vary between conventional and automatic equipment and are not stated per row in the exported CSV files, temporal_support remains unknown across all twenty series.

docs.title: Stage references, coordinates, and metadata
docs.text:
River stage (nivel) is published in centimetres (cm) relative to the local staff-gauge zero (cero del limnímetro or cota cero in IDEAM's hydrometric manuals). RivRetrieve multiplies cm values by 0.01 to return metres (m), preserves "cm" in source_unit (with "m3/s" on discharge), and sets vertical_reference="gauge_zero" on all ten stage series. Genuine zero flows (0.0 m3/s), zero stages (0.0 m), and negative stages below local gauge zero are preserved without clamping.

IDEAM's open-data CSV exports and station registry do not publish local gauge-zero elevations relative to sea level or dated histories of staff-gauge relocations. As a result, vertical_datum is unknown on all stage series. Do not add a station's general elevation (Altitud) to gauge_zero stage readings to estimate water-surface elevation above sea level.

Station metadata (rr.metadata(selection)) exposes three fields from IDEAM's station catalogue (catalogo.csv):

  • Nombre as station_name
  • Corriente as water_body_name
  • Altitud as elevation (published as numeric text without an explicit unit or vertical datum in catalogo.csv, so elevation_unit and elevation_datum remain null in the packaged metadata)

IDEAM's station catalogue does not publish catchment drainage areas, so drainage_area_* columns are null. Horizontal coordinates (Latitud and Longitud) are decimal degrees in Colombia, but because neither catalogo.csv nor its Socrata schema specifies whether coordinates refer to MAGNA-SIRGAS (EPSG:4686), WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), or unprojected legacy Observatorio de Bogotá surveys, crs is "unknown".

docs.title: Record currency and local caching
docs.text:
IDEAM regenerates active S3 CSV files daily from AQUARIUS. Active telemetric gauges commonly extend to within one to three days of the current date, whereas conventional or decommissioned gauges end earlier. Each S3 request downloads the complete historical CSV file for one (station, series) pair (ranging from single-row 85-byte files up to roughly 35 MB on multi-decade hourly series).

When cache="reuse" is passed to rr.fetch:

  • RivRetrieve caches the series over its observed [first_observation, last_observation] span. Subsequent queries whose requested window falls inside that span are served offline from the local store with zero network requests.
  • Requesting dates after last_observation (or before first_observation) triggers a fresh download of the S3 CSV file and updates any revised provisional values across the overlapping period. Because pre-record and post-record sub-spans are not marked complete in the local store, queries for future or newly published days are never blocked by stale empty-window cache entries.
  • If you want to pick up in-place recalculations of provisional values inside an already cached date span without extending the query end date, pass cache="refresh".

When a requested S3 CSV object returns HTTP 404 (NoSuchKey), RivRetrieve reports a source.http_not_found warning in result.issues, leaves sibling stations and series unaffected, and retains any previously cached observations in the local store rather than erasing them during transient S3 export rebuilds.

docs.title: Time and data status
docs.text:
Every S3 CSV row carries an unqualified wall-clock timestamp fechaObservacion formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS with no UTC offset. Outside 1992 and 1993, Colombia uses standard civil time UTC-05:00 year-round. Between May 1992 and February 1993, Colombia observed one hour of daylight saving time (Hora Gaviria, UTC-04:00 under Decreto 591 de 1992). IDEAM's AQUARIUS exporter formatted stored timestamps in historical local civil time without offsets:

  • During May 1992 through early February 1993, daily, monthly, and yearly rows carry 01:00:00 instead of 00:00:00, and conventional 06:00/18:00 readings shift to 07:00/19:00.
  • When clocks fell back on 1993-02-06 23:00:00, hourly series (CAUDAL_H, NIVEL_H) can contain two distinct consecutive measurements stamped with the identical wall-clock string 1993-02-06 23:00:00.

Because an offset-free timestamp cannot disambiguate the folded 1993-02-06 23:00:00 hour and IDEAM's open documentation does not state the exact hydrological day boundary across historical conventional and automatic eras, RivRetrieve sets time_zone="unknown" and leaves day_definition, timestamp_anchor, and label_time unknown across all twenty series. rr.to_utc() refuses unknown time zones rather than guessing an offset on ambiguous wall-clock timestamps, and duplicate 1993-02-06 23:00:00 rows are preserved in source order.

Date and timestamp clipping follows each series's time resolution:

  • Daily series (*_D): Clipped by calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD), so 1992-08-01 01:00:00 is matched as calendar date 1992-08-01 alongside ordinary 00:00:00 daily rows.
  • Sub-daily (CAUDAL_H, NIVEL_H), monthly (*_M), and yearly (*_A) series: Clipped by exact source timestamp. Monthly series are stamped on the first day of the month (YYYY-MM-01 00:00:00, or 01:00:00 during 1992-1993), and yearly series are stamped on January 1 (YYYY-01-01 00:00:00, or 1993-01-01 01:00:00); include those first-of-period dates in [start, end] when requesting monthly or yearly summaries.

Each S3 CSV row includes a third column, nivelAprobacion, carrying IDEAM's AQUARIUS approval status:

  • Preliminar: provisional operational data (AQUARIUS approval level 900), subject to rating-curve and quality-control revision.
  • En revisión: data currently under hydrographic review (level 1100).
  • Definitivo: validated archival data (level 1200).
  • "" (empty string): legacy ungraded rows in some older series.

Separate AQUARIUS Grade markers in IDEAM's open exports remain unpopulated (50 - INDEFINIDO). Following RivRetrieve's library-wide convention, rr.fetch returns observations across all nivelAprobacion states without filtering or modifying values. The nivelAprobacion value is preserved per row as a source annotation (schema co_ideam.s3, observation scope):

result = rr.fetch(selection, start="2010-01-01", end="2010-01-07")

# Field catalogue
print(rr.annotations(result).select("schema", "name", "dtype").rows())
# [('co_ideam.s3', 'nivelAprobacion', 'String')]

# Append to the canonical frame
annotated = result.to_polars(annotations=True)
print(annotated.select("time", "value", "nivelAprobacion").head(3).rows())

Missing dates and hours are simply absent from IDEAM's CSV files rather than written as placeholder rows.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
IDEAM's Socrata open-data metadata cards for the hydrological station catalogue and the twenty historical discharge and stage series declare the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0) licence (CC_40_BY_SA) with mandatory attribution to IDEAM:

Instituto de Hidrología, Meteorología y Estudios Ambientales - IDEAM, Bogotá D.C.

Under CC BY-SA 4.0, you may copy, redistribute, and adapt the data for any purpose, including commercial use, provided that you credit IDEAM, link to the licence, indicate if changes were made, and distribute any adapted material under the same CC BY-SA 4.0 licence (ShareAlike). Both rr.describe("co_ideam") and result.provenance expose license="Creative Commons Attribution | Share Alike 4.0 International" and citation="Instituto de Hidrología, Meteorología y Estudios Ambientales - IDEAM, Bogotá D.C.". For scientific reproducibility, also record the ten-digit station code, published series code (such as Q_MEDIA_D), requested period, and retrieval date.

RivRetrieve paces requests to datos.ideam.gov.co at a maximum of one request per second. Use cache="reuse" when running repeated analyses across many stations or multi-decade records.

The empty tuple () means that retrieval reported no issues; it does not establish the quality of the values. docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
CHMI establishes and operates state monitoring networks for the atmosphere and hydrosphere and processes their measurements. It publishes data from the national hydrometeorological database through its open-data service. This institutional role does not identify the operator of every station in the published catalogue.

For each station and calendar year, CHMI publishes separate files for daily and hourly observations. The daily file can contain mean discharge, stage and water temperature; the hourly file can contain mean discharge and stage. A file need not contain every quantity. For example, the daily file used above contains discharge and stage for 2020, but no water temperature.

Select a station using CHMI's station identifier, such as 0-203-1-180100 for VD České Údolí. RivRetrieve keeps these source identifiers unchanged.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge QD Daily Mean m³/s m³/s stage HD Daily Mean cm m temperature TD Daily Mean °C °C discharge QH Hourly Mean m³/s m³/s stage HH Hourly Mean cm m

Select frequency="daily" or frequency="hourly", with statistic="mean". CHMI's dataset description defines these as mean daily values (průměrné denní hodnoty) and mean hourly values (průměrné hodinové hodnoty). RivRetrieve converts stage from centimetres to metres. Discharge and water temperature need no unit conversion. Stage is water level; RivRetrieve has not established its vertical reference or datum.

The catalogue lists all five series at each station because the station metadata does not state which of these quantities are available. A station being listed does not guarantee data for every quantity or requested period.

docs.title: How far back, and how recent
docs.text:
Availability depends on the annual files CHMI has published for a station and on the series within those files. RivRetrieve reads only the historical service, so requests cannot provide observations more recent than its published records. There is no fixed latest year imposed by RivRetrieve.

CHMI also publishes current observations in its recent and now folders and additional historical series that RivRetrieve does not yet read. Making these available is on the roadmap (#294).

docs.title: Time and data status
docs.text:
CHMI's historical observation timestamps carry a UTC Z suffix. RivRetrieve returns their wall-clock labels in time, paired with time_zone="+00:00". Daily values have midnight labels. The boundaries of the averaging day are unknown, so do not assume a daily mean covers midnight to midnight UTC. Hourly values are published means, but whether their labels mark the start or end of the averaging hour is also unknown.

The historical records read here carry timestamps and values without observation-level quality or approval flags. Being in the historical service does not by itself establish a value's validation status. RivRetrieve makes no quality judgement of its own.

A published null remains a row with value=null. A date without a published observation supplies no row. A failed request remains an issue alongside any successful records. Check issues before interpreting an empty result.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
CHMI's open-data page states that its open data can be used free of charge under Creative Commons BY 4.0. Retrieval requires no personal credentials.

Its disclaimer and conditions of use state:

Produkty Českého hydrometeorologického ústavu dostupné na těchto webových stránkách podléhají licenci Creative Commons 4.0 CC-BY. Dílo smíte sdílet a upravovat za podmínky uvedení původu (zdroje ČHMÚ).

In English, unofficially: CHMI's products available on these websites are licensed under Creative Commons 4.0 CC BY; you may share and adapt the work on condition that you credit the origin (the source, ČHMÚ).

No formatted data citation was identified in these terms. Credit ČHMÚ and retain the station, quantity, requested period and access date to make the retrieved record traceable. This is practical guidance, not a CHMI citation template.

docs.text:

RivRetrieve reads VandA's public API. Retrieve one week of discharge at station 25003918, Skjern Å at Gjaldbæk Bro:

import rivretrieve as rr

result = rr.fetch(selection, start="2026-11-08", end="2026-11-14T23:59:59", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)

print([(issue.severity, issue.code) for issue in result.issues])

Output:

2026-11-08T00:10:00.000000,+00:00,17.2126,m3/s
2026-11-08T00:20:00.000000,+00:00,17.2126,m3/s
881
[]

The request returned 881 readings in m³/s, about ten minutes apart, for the seven-day window. The preview shows the first three. The empty issue list means retrieval reported no problems; it does not establish the quality of the values. cache="bypass" requests VandA's API rather than a local cache. This output was checked live on 2026-11-15; published values can change, and VandA's native reading interval is set per station, so a later retrieval or a different station need not reproduce this exact spacing. See Usage for general selection and result handling.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
Danmarks Miljøportal (the Danish Environmental Data Portal) publishes VandA's station registry and observations. Its own open-data catalogue record states that this dataset is covered by Miljøportalens "dataansvarsaftale" (data- responsibility agreement), specifically Annex 2, "Det rene overfladevand" ("clean surface water"). That agreement names the data owners ("Dataejer") as "Kommunerne, Miljøstyrelsen": Denmark's municipalities and Miljøstyrelsen (the Danish Environmental Protection Agency). Danmarks Miljøportal is the publisher that distributes the data on the owners' behalf, not the measuring body itself.

VandA's own station registry additionally lists a station owner and a field operator for each station (for example, station 25003918 lists Miljøstyrelsen as owner and DCE, Aarhus University as operator). RivRetrieve's catalogue does not currently surface these per-station fields.

Station coordinates are RivRetrieve's own reprojection of VandA's native coordinates (ETRS89 / UTM zone 32N, EPSG:25832) to EPSG:4326. VandA does not publish latitude and longitude directly.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge Vandføring, result Unknown Unknown l/s m³/s stage Vandstand, result Unknown Unknown cm m stage Vandstand, DVR90-corrected, resultElevationCorrected Unknown Unknown cm m temperature Temperaturmåling, result Unknown Unknown °C °C

RivRetrieve converts discharge from litres per second to cubic metres per second and stage from centimetres to metres. Water temperature needs no conversion. VandA publishes no named aggregation for any of these readings, so RivRetrieve leaves frequency and statistic unknown rather than inferring one from the reading interval.

Stage is published as two parallel fields for every reading: result and resultElevationCorrected. Both describe the same measured water level; they differ in vertical reference. resultElevationCorrected is stated, and independently confirmed against VandA's own benchmark ("Kotemåling") readings at two stations, to be an elevation above sea level in the DVR90 vertical datum (Dansk Vertikal Reference 1990, Denmark's national height system). The raw result field is a reading relative to the station's own local gauge zero; VandA does not state what that gauge zero is referenced to, and this port found the full published field description and the examination-type configuration both silent on a datum for it. Its relationship to sea level, and whether its gauge zero is consistent across stations, are unestablished by the source.

The catalogue holds 1,565 stations. A snapshot check of recorded availability (2026-11-14) found numerical discharge values at 294 stations, stage at 1,373, and water temperature at 66; the remaining stations are catalogued with unknown availability for that quantity, not confirmed absent. A station being listed does not guarantee data for every quantity or requested period.

docs.title: Series selection
docs.text:
Stage is the one quantity with more than one selectable series: result and resultElevationCorrected are both returned under quantity="stage", and selecting one is required to interpret the vertical reference correctly. Inspect the candidates before choosing, and select the corrected field explicitly:

stage = rr.find(provider="dk_vanda", station="25003918", quantity="stage")

candidates = rr.series(stage)
corrected = rr.pick(stage, variant="resultElevationCorrected")

result = rr.fetch(corrected, start="2026-11-14", end="2026-11-14T23:59:59", cache="bypass")
print(result.data.select("time", "value", "unit").head(2).write_csv(float_precision=3), end="")

Output:

time,value,unit
2026-11-14T00:00:00.000000,4.335,m
2026-11-14T00:10:00.000000,4.336,m

The same station's raw result field for the same instants reads 0.626 m and 0.627 m: a real difference of about 3.7 m, consistent with a fixed benchmark offset between the station's local gauge zero and the DVR90 elevation, not a measurement disagreement. Without variant, a stage selection covers both fields; fetching without picking one returns rows for both (278 rows for the one-day window above, 139 per field), distinguished by the series_id column or by inspecting candidates above. See Series selection in the usage guide for the general pattern.

docs.title: How far back, and how recent
docs.text:
VandA's historical depth is set per station and per quantity; RivRetrieve's packaged catalogue does not record a first or last available date for dk_vanda, so it cannot tell you a station's depth in advance. Depth varies widely: this page's example station, 25003918, has continuous discharge telemetry back to 1975-01-01. Other stations have telemetry reaching back only to 2023 or 2025, with no earlier continuous record under any examination type. A request for a station and period with no published reading returns no rows for that period; it does not establish that the station has no data at all.

To check a specific station's practical depth before requesting a long historical window, query VandA's own station endpoint (GET https://vandah.miljoeportal.dk/api/stations?stationId=<id>), which lists each examination type's first and latest published result directly; this is a plain, unauthenticated metadata lookup, not an observation request. A single failed attempt at a genuinely old window is not conclusive either: a request decades in the past occasionally times out or returns a server error on a first attempt and succeeds on an immediate retry, which looks like a transient, cold-query slowdown rather than missing data.

VandA separately tracks manual field gaugings (spot measurements, not a continuous series) as their own examination type. Some stations with little or no continuous telemetry history still have decades of field gaugings. RivRetrieve does not catalogue or retrieve field gaugings as a product; only continuous telemetry is available through dk_vanda.

docs.title: Time and data status
docs.text:
VandA publishes every timestamp as a UTC instant. RivRetrieve returns these in time, paired with time_zone="+00:00". Timestamps mark the measurement instant; readings are point-in-time values, not a stated average over a period.

Water temperature readings can carry a non-null reason code (reasonSc) from VandA's own vocabulary, paired with a free-text reason. RivRetrieve preserves both verbatim in the dk_vanda.temperature annotation schema (Int64 and String, nullable); it does not interpret or rank the code, because VandA's own published reason-code vocabulary states no textual meaning for any code. Discharge and stage responses never carry this field.

temp = rr.find(provider="dk_vanda", station="70000277", quantity="temperature")
result = rr.fetch(temp, start="2026-11-08", end="2026-11-08T23:59:59", cache="bypass")
print(rr.annotations(result).select("schema", "name", "dtype").rows())

annotated = result.to_polars(annotations=True)
print(annotated.select("value", "reasonSc", "reason").head(3).rows())

Output:

[('dk_vanda.temperature', 'reasonSc', 'Int64'), ('dk_vanda.temperature', 'reason', 'String')]
[(8.3, None, None), (8.3, None, None), (8.2, None, None)]

This station and window happen to carry no non-null reason; the columns are still present and nullable, so a flagged reading elsewhere carries the same shape without changing it. Checked live on 2026-11-15.

Pass annotations="reasonSc" or annotations=["reasonSc", "reason"] to result.to_polars(...) or result.to_pandas(...) when you only want specific columns, or call rr.annotations(result, schema="dk_vanda.temperature") for the native schema table. See Source annotations for the general pattern.

A published null remains a row with value=null. A period with no published reading supplies no row. A failed request remains an issue alongside any successful records. Check issues before interpreting an empty result.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
Danmarks Miljøportal's own dataset catalogue record states, in its structured metadata (dct:license) and again on the dataset's landing page:

Licens: Creative Common - CC0 1.0

CC0 1.0 (Creative Commons Zero) dedicates the data to the public domain and does not require attribution. For traceability, this port's catalogue cites the publisher as "Danmarks Miljøportal" and the data owners as the municipalities and Miljøstyrelsen (the Danish Environmental Protection Agency), matching the dataset's own data-responsibility agreement. Retrieval requires no credentials.

Separately, Miljøportal's portal-wide terms of use ask that catalogue data carry the generic sentence "Indeholder data, som benyttes i henhold til vilkår for brug af danske offentlige data" ("Contains data used under the terms of use for Danish public data"); it is not specific to this dataset, and this dataset's own explicit, twice-stated CC0 marking takes precedence.

docs.title: Finland: Syke
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider fi_syke Country Finland Published by Suomen ympäristökeskus (Syke), the Finnish Environment Institute Read from Syke's Hydrologiarajapinta OData hydrology interface (rajapinnat.ymparisto.fi) Quantities Daily discharge, stage and surface water temperature Stations in the catalogue 2,543. Availability depends on quantity Station metadata Station name and water-body name. See Fields by provider Credentials None Licence stated by Syke Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) Agency documentation Syke open data and web services

RivRetrieve reads Syke's Hydrologiarajapinta OData service. Retrieve one week of published daily discharge at station 894, Ruskeakoski on the Jänisjoki:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="fi_syke",
    station="894",
    quantity="discharge",
)

result = rr.fetch(selection, start="2020-01-01", end="2020-01-07", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print(result.issues)

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2020-01-01T00:00:00.000000,unknown,16.73,m3/s
2020-01-02T00:00:00.000000,unknown,17.79,m3/s
2020-01-03T00:00:00.000000,unknown,19.02,m3/s
7
()

The request returned seven daily values in m³/s, one for each date from January 1 to 7. The preview shows the first three. The empty tuple () means retrieval reported no issues; it does not establish the quality of the values. time_zone is unknown because Syke's timestamps carry no UTC offset. All three fi_syke series have frequency="daily", and the request did not restrict by statistic because Syke's service does not state whether a daily value is a mean, an instantaneous reading, or another statistic.

cache="bypass" requests Syke's service rather than a local cache. This output was checked live on 2026-11-08. Published values can change, so a later retrieval need not reproduce this output exactly. See Usage for general selection and result handling.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
Syke operates Finland's national hydrology API and publishes station and observation data through it. Some of the stations in the catalogue are measured by Syke directly; others are measured by regional ELY-centres (Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment) or other bodies that report into Syke's systems. The API does not publish an operator field per station, so RivRetrieve cannot state who measures a particular station; it publishes what Syke publishes.

Station identifiers are Syke's own per-installation site identifier (Paikka_Id), confirmed against Syke's public map service and against the independently published CAMELS-FI dataset, both of which key on the same identifier. In Syke's station table (Paikka), each Paikka_Id is associated with one of the three admitted quantities: a river gauge with both discharge and stage readings appears as two separate Paikka_Id stations in the catalogue, one per quantity, rather than one station with two available products.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge Virtaama Daily Unknown m³/s m³/s stage Vedenkorkeus Daily Unknown cm m temperature LampoPintavesi Daily Unknown °C °C

The source field is the Hydrologiarajapinta OData entity-set name, where each row's numeric reading is published in Arvo. Each quantity has one daily series per station, so variant stays unset (variant=None). RivRetrieve converts stage from centimetres to metres; discharge and surface water temperature need no unit conversion. All three series have frequency="daily", whereas statistic is unknown because Syke's documentation and metadata tables do not state whether a published daily value is a mean, an instantaneous reading, or another aggregation. Do not filter by statistic="mean" when selecting fi_syke series.

Stage is an absolute water-surface elevation relative to a Finnish national height datum, not a small reading relative to a local gauge zero: published stage values range from about -2 m to +245 m, consistent with Finland's coast-to-inland relief (vertical_reference="above_sea_level"). Which of Finland's historical national height systems (such as N2000, N60, NN, or N43) a given reading is expressed in is not stated on observation rows, so vertical_datum remains None and RivRetrieve does not apply Syke's separate per-station datum-offset table (VedenkTasoTieto).

Depth-profile water temperature soundings (LampoLuotaus, which vary by measurement depth) and catchment runoff series (Valuma) are not included in fi_syke.

In Syke's Paikka table, 711 stations are witnessed for discharge, 1,753 for stage, and 79 for temperature. The packaged catalogue records availability="available" for a station's witnessed quantity and availability="unknown" (rather than "unavailable") for the other two quantities. Because RivRetrieve keeps pairs with "unknown" availability selectable, pass quantity when selecting a station so the selection targets only that quantity, and note that a provider-wide query such as rr.find(provider="fi_syke", quantity="discharge") includes both the 711 stations witnessed for discharge and the remaining stations whose discharge availability is "unknown". A station being listed does not guarantee data for every requested period.

docs.title: How far back, and how recent
docs.text:
Coverage varies by station. The example station, 894, has published discharge back to January 1, 1959. Some stations hold decades of history; others have shorter or more recent records. RivRetrieve reads whatever range Syke currently publishes for a station; there is no fixed earliest or latest date imposed by RivRetrieve. Checked live on 2026-11-08, several active stations had daily values published within the preceding one to two days.

A request for a period with no published observation returns no rows for that period rather than an issue. It does not establish that the station never had data in that period.

docs.title: Time and data status
docs.text:
Syke's timestamps carry no time zone marker, and the agency's documentation does not state one. RivRetrieve returns the published wall-clock label in time paired with time_zone="unknown". Do not assume these timestamps are UTC, Finnish local time, or any other specific zone.

Some discharge and stage readings carry Syke's integer flag key Lippu_id, which points into Syke's Lippu reference table covering mixed meanings: data-quality notes (for example, interpolated or reduced values), statistical summaries, model-simulated values, and device identifiers. RivRetrieve exposes Lippu_id verbatim on discharge and stage results in the fi_syke.observations annotation schema without dropping flagged rows or ranking one code above another. Pass annotations=True to result.to_polars(...) or result.to_pandas(...) to project Lippu_id, or call rr.annotations(result) to inspect schema metadata. Surface water temperature (water_temperature_reported) carries no Lippu_id field and emits no observation annotations. See Source annotations for general options.

Some older discharge and stage readings also carry a published minimum and maximum alongside the daily value; current readings do not. RivRetrieve does not return these minimum and maximum fields, since Syke does not state what they represent.

A published null remains a row with value=null. A date without a published observation supplies no row. A failed request remains an issue alongside any successful records. Check issues before interpreting an empty result.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
Syke's open-data terms state:

Open data distributed by the Finnish Environment Institute (Syke) is licenced under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence. The data covered by the license can be freely used in any way, provided that the source of the data is mentioned: the name of the licensor and the name of the data.

Syke's worked example of attribution reads "Source: Finnish Environment Institute (Syke)". Retrieval requires no personal credentials.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Publisher pages checked on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08:

  • Syke open data and web services: the Hydrologiarajapinta OData interface.
  • Syke open-data use license and responsibilities: licence and attribution.
  • Syke's public map service (paikkatiedot.ymparisto.fi): independent confirmation of Paikka_Id as the per-station identifier.

docs.title: France: Hub'Eau
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider fr_hubeau Country Hydrometry: metropolitan and overseas France; temperature: metropolitan France Published by Hub'Eau (hubeau.eaufrance.fr) Variables Discharge, stage, water temperature Stations in the catalogue 7,347 (6,475 hydrometry and 872 temperature). Availability depends on quantity and period Station metadata Station name, water-body name, drainage area and elevation. See Fields by provider Credentials None Licence stated by Hub'Eau Licence ouverte Etalab Agency documentation Hub'Eau hydrometry API, Hub'Eau river temperature API

Retrieve published daily mean discharge at station Y251002001, L'Orb à Bédarieux:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="fr_hubeau",
    station="Y251002001",
    quantity="discharge",
    frequency="daily",
    statistic="mean",
)

result = rr.fetch(selection, start="2024-01-01", end="2024-01-07", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(float_precision=3), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print(result.issues)
print(rr.annotations(result).select("name", "dtype").rows())

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000,unknown,1.159,m3/s
2024-01-02T00:00:00.000000,unknown,1.144,m3/s
2024-01-03T00:00:00.000000,unknown,1.159,m3/s
7
()
[('code_statut', 'Int64'), ('libelle_statut', 'String'), ('code_qualification', 'Int64'), ('libelle_qualification', 'String'), ('code_methode', 'Int64'), ('libelle_methode', 'String')]

The request returned seven daily values, the six fr_hubeau.obs_elab annotation fields, and no retrieval issues (the empty tuple ()). An empty issue tuple does not mean the source has approved the quality of the values. The values are source-published daily means, returned in m³/s. RivRetrieve does not calculate them from instantaneous observations. Bare dates include the whole first and last day. cache="bypass" requests the source rather than a local cache. The preview shows the first three values, rounded to three decimal places. unknown means RivRetrieve has not established the time zone of these daily labels. Source values can change, so a later retrieval need not reproduce this output exactly. See Usage for selection options and working with returned data.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
France's hydrometric records bring together measurements from regional environmental authorities (DREAL) and other national and local producers. The Service Central Vigicrues runs the national hydrometry platform, PHyC. Records cover metropolitan France and overseas territories; availability and record length vary by station.

Hub'Eau provides open APIs for French water data. It is a collaboration between the French biodiversity agency (OFB) and BRGM, the French geological survey.

RivRetrieve reads published daily discharge and stage from Hub'Eau's hydrometry API. Water temperature follows a separate route: Hub'Eau's river-temperature API distributes records from Naïades for metropolitan France. It is not part of the PHyC hydrometric network.

Hub'Eau's name does not identify the original producer of every measurement. This matters when citing a dataset (see Terms and citation).

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Select provider="fr_hubeau" for daily hydrometry and temperature. For station-own instantaneous discharge and stage, use the separate HydroPortail provider. The services retain separate station inventories, source identities and terms.

Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge QmnJ Daily Mean l/s m³/s discharge QIXnJ Daily Maximum l/s m³/s stage HIXnJ Daily Maximum mm m temperature resultat, parameter 1301 Unknown Unknown °C °C

These source fields identify the published observations; there is no separate variant to choose for these Hub'Eau products.

RivRetrieve converts discharge from litres per second to cubic metres per second, and stage from millimetres to metres. Temperature is already in °C. The daily maxima are maxima of instantaneous values, not maxima of daily means. RivRetrieve does not calculate additional daily statistics from instantaneous records.

A station being listed does not guarantee that it has data for every quantity or requested period. Hub'Eau describes daily hydrometric records reaching back to 1900 at some stations.

docs.title: Stations and sites
docs.text:
A site is a reach of river where discharge measurements are considered homogeneous and comparable. A station is a measuring installation within that site. It can provide stage, discharge, or both.

One site can hold several stations. Keep the station identifier when selecting observations; a site and a station are different source identities.

Temperature comes from a separate monitoring network. Do not assume that a station selected for discharge also provides temperature.

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
The example's time column contains daily dates represented at midnight. Its time_zone="unknown" means that RivRetrieve has not established the clock defining the start and end of those days. Hub'Eau describes its hydrometric dates as UTC, but that statement alone does not establish which 24 hours a daily value covers.

Temperature observations have separate source date and clock fields. Their time zone is also unknown. RivRetrieve has not established whether each value represents an instant or an interval, or what sampling or averaging period applies.

docs.title: Data status
docs.text:
Hub'Eau publishes qualification, status, and method fields alongside observations. RivRetrieve retains those verbatim fields in two observation-grain schemas without turning them into a quality ranking:

  • fr_hubeau.obs_elab (hydrometry daily/monthly series): code_statut (Int64), libelle_statut (String), code_qualification (Int64), libelle_qualification (String), code_methode (Int64), and libelle_methode (String).
  • fr_hubeau.temperature_chronique (continuous temperature series): code_qualification (String) and libelle_qualification (String).

Use rr.annotations(result) to list attached fields and result.to_polars(annotations=True) or result.to_pandas(annotations=True) to project them onto returned rows. Because code_qualification has type Int64 in fr_hubeau.obs_elab and String in fr_hubeau.temperature_chronique, narrow a mixed hydrometry-and-temperature result with rr.pick(...) before calling to_polars(annotations=True), or read each table directly with rr.annotations(result, schema=...). See Usage for details on inspecting and exporting source annotations, and receipts to retain raw publisher bytes.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
Hub'Eau's terms of use, section 5.1.3, state:

La réutilisation des Jeux de données est régie par la licence ouverte Etalab, https://www.etalab.gouv.fr/licence-ouverte-open-licence. Les Jeux de données sont donc librement et gratuitement utilisables et réutilisables, y compris dans un but commercial. L'utilisateur de ces données doit néanmoins veiller à citer l'auteur des Jeux de données.

In English, unofficially: reuse is governed by the Etalab open licence, including commercial reuse, and requires citation of the dataset author. The linked Licence Ouverte 2.0 requires the source (at least the licensor) and the last-update date of the reused information. A retrieval date does not necessarily establish that last-update date.

Hub'Eau distributes data from several producers. Cite the dataset author rather than assuming the API operator produced every observation. No ready-made citation string was identified in its terms.

These terms apply to the Hub'Eau route. They do not establish the terms of the separate HydroPortail service. Hub'Eau retrieval requires no personal credentials in RivRetrieve.

docs.title: France: HydroPortail
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider fr_hydroportail Country Metropolitan and overseas France Published by HydroPortail (hydro.eaufrance.fr), Service Central Vigicrues Variables Instantaneous discharge and stage Stations in the catalogue 6,409. Availability depends on quantity, source selection and period Station metadata Coordinates only. See Fields by provider Credentials None Terms Reuse licence and standard citation not established Agency documentation HydroPortail help

Retrieve instantaneous discharge at station Y251002001, L'Orb à Bédarieux, selecting HydroPortail's validated records:

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="fr_hydroportail",
    station="Y251002001",
    quantity="discharge",
    statistic="instantaneous",
)
validated = rr.pick(selection, variant="validated")

result = rr.fetch(validated, start="2020-01-01", end="2020-01-02", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit").head(3)
print(preview.write_csv(float_precision=3), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print([(issue.severity, issue.code) for issue in result.issues])

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2020-01-01T00:01:00.000000,+00:00,13.500,m3/s
2020-01-01T00:20:00.000000,+00:00,13.300,m3/s
2020-01-01T00:55:00.000000,+00:00,13.700,m3/s
50
[('info', 'provenance.license_not_established'), ('info', 'provenance.citation_not_established')]

The preview shows the first three instantaneous values in m³/s, rounded to three decimal places. The request returned 50 rows. Their timestamps need not be evenly spaced; RivRetrieve does not fill gaps or calculate daily means. Bare dates include the whole first and last day. cache="bypass" requests the source rather than a local cache. Source values can change, so a later retrieval need not reproduce this output exactly.

The two informational issues mean that RivRetrieve has not established a reuse licence or standard citation for these records. They do not mean that the observation request failed. See Terms and citation before reusing the data.

Run the examples below in the same Python session. See Usage for general selection options and working with returned data.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
France's hydrometric records bring together measurements from regional environmental authorities (DREAL) and other national and local producers. The Service Central Vigicrues runs the national hydrometry platform, PHyC. Records cover metropolitan France and overseas territories; availability and record length vary by station.

HydroPortail is the national hydrometry portal, published by the Service Central Vigicrues. It replaced the former Banque HYDRO interfaces in January 2022. Its name does not identify the original producer of every historical measurement.

RivRetrieve reads station-own instantaneous stage and discharge from HydroPortail. Published daily hydrometry and Naïades water temperature are available through the separate Hub'Eau provider. The services retain separate station inventories, source identities and terms. Temperature comes from a separate monitoring network.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit discharge Q; four selectors below Unknown Instantaneous l/s m³/s stage H; four selectors below Unknown Instantaneous mm m

Both quantities are instantaneous. Each source field supports the same four variant selectors: raw, validated, pre_validated_and_validated, and most_valid. Choose a selector as shown below.

RivRetrieve converts discharge from litres per second to cubic metres per second, and stage from millimetres to metres. It does not calculate additional daily statistics from instantaneous records.

A station being listed does not guarantee that it has data for every quantity, source selection or requested period. Historical instantaneous records are available, but their length varies by station. A successful short request does not establish continuous coverage of the station's history.

docs.title: Stations and sites
docs.text:
A site is a reach of river where discharge measurements are considered homogeneous and comparable. A station is a measuring installation within that site. It can provide stage, discharge, or both.

One site can hold several stations. HydroPortail states that at most one is active at a time for producing the site's discharge. RivRetrieve retrieves the selected station's own record, rather than the site's combined discharge record.

docs.title: Time
docs.text: For instantaneous values retrieved from HydroPortail, time contains UTC clock labels and time_zone is +00:00. Read the two columns together: the datetime column itself does not carry a time zone.

docs.title: Data status and source selections
docs.text:
HydroPortail exposes four source selections through variant:

Selector Requested source selection raw Raw records validated Validated records pre_validated_and_validated Pre-validated and validated records together most_valid HydroPortail's most-valid selection

Inspect the catalogue candidates before choosing:

print(sorted(rr.series(selection)["variant"].to_list()))
print(rr.series(validated).select("station_id", "variant").rows())

Output:

['most_valid', 'pre_validated_and_validated', 'raw', 'validated']
[('Y251002001', 'validated')]

Use pick to choose a selector, then fetch to retrieve its observations. For example, request HydroPortail's most-valid selection:

most_valid = rr.pick(selection, variant="most_valid")

most_valid_result = rr.fetch(
    most_valid, start="2020-01-01", end="2020-01-02", cache="bypass"
)

print(rr.series(most_valid_result).select("station_id", "variant").rows())
print(most_valid_result.data.height)
print([(issue.severity, issue.code) for issue in most_valid_result.issues])

Output:

[('Y251002001', 'most_valid')]
50
[('info', 'provenance.license_not_established'), ('info', 'provenance.citation_not_established')]

Fetching selection without pick requests all four selectors and keeps their records separate. Availability can differ by selector and period. An explicit choice requests only that selector; RivRetrieve does not substitute another one when no observations are returned.

most_valid is HydroPortail's selection, not a RivRetrieve quality ranking. Its exact selection algorithm has not been established. The combined selector includes pre-validated and validated records. This public route does not provide corrected-only or pre-validated-only histories.

The variant selector chooses which record stream HydroPortail returns. Each returned observation also carries HydroPortail's point-level numeric codes in the fr_hydroportail.series annotation schema (Int64, nullable):

  • s: processing status (statut, such as 4 raw, 8 corrected, 12 pre-validated, 16 validated).
  • q: qualification (qualification, such as 12 doubtful, 16 unqualified, 20 good).
  • m: observation method (méthode, such as 0 measured, 4 reconstituted, 8 calculated, 10 expert-reviewed).
  • c: continuity (continuité, such as 0 continuous, 1 discontinuous, 4 weak discontinuity, 8 strong discontinuity).

The requested variant and per-point codes play different roles. Mixed selectors such as pre_validated_and_validated and most_valid can combine points with different statuses (for example s=4 raw points alongside s=16 validated points) within one stream, and even a validated stream can mark individual points doubtful (q=12). RivRetrieve preserves the published integer codes without ranking or filtering observations. HydroPortail's glossary defines the underlying concepts.

Inspect the annotation field catalog on result and project those columns onto the validated discharge rows fetched above:

print(rr.annotations(result).select("schema", "name", "dtype").rows())

annotated = result.to_polars(annotations=True)
print(annotated.select("s", "q", "m", "c").head(2).rows())

Output:

[('fr_hydroportail.series', 's', 'Int64'), ('fr_hydroportail.series', 'q', 'Int64'), ('fr_hydroportail.series', 'm', 'Int64'), ('fr_hydroportail.series', 'c', 'Int64')]
[(16, 12, 10, 0), (16, 12, 10, 0)]

The first output lists the four nullable integer fields attached to result. In the two projected discharge rows (13.500 and 13.300 m³/s from validated), each observation carries validated status (s=16), doubtful qualification (q=12), expert-reviewed method (m=10), and continuous continuity (c=0).

Pass annotations="q" or annotations=["s", "q"] to result.to_polars(...) or result.to_pandas(...) when you only want specific columns, or call rr.annotations(result, schema="fr_hydroportail.series") for the native schema table. Window-level response summaries and chart overlays (such as statistics and correctionCurves), as well as unpopulated md fields, are omitted from observation annotations. Retain full response bytes with optional receipts when raw payload records matter. See Source annotations and Series inspection and result views for general result and issue inspection.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
HydroPortail provides public access without personal credentials in RivRetrieve. Its legal and FAQ pages do not establish a reuse licence or standard citation for station records. Hub'Eau's Etalab terms apply to the Hub'Eau route and must not be assumed to cover HydroPortail retrievals.

Publication by HydroPortail does not establish the original author of every historical measurement. RivRetrieve reports the unknown licence and citation as informational issues, including when observations are returned successfully. Check the applicable terms and attribution with the publisher before reusing these records.

docs.title: Japan: MLIT
docs.text:
Documentation index · Usage

Provider jp_mlit Country Japan Published by Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) Read from 水文水質データベース, the Water Information System (www1.river.go.jp) Quantities Discharge and stage, hourly and daily Stations in the catalogue 1,023. Availability depends on quantity and period Station metadata Station name, water-body name, drainage area and elevation. See Fields by provider Credentials No personal credentials required Terms Numerical data may be used freely; automated access has separate restrictions (see below) Agency documentation 水文水質データベース, 利用上の注意 (notes on use)

Retrieve two days of published daily discharge at station 305071285512040. Read Automated access and caching before running requests.

import rivretrieve as rr

selection = rr.find(
    provider="jp_mlit",
    station="305071285512040",
    quantity="discharge",
    frequency="daily",
)

result = rr.fetch(selection, start="2020-01-10", end="2020-01-11", cache="bypass")

preview = result.data.select("time", "time_zone", "value", "unit")
print(preview.write_csv(), end="")

print(result.data.height)
print(rr.annotations(result).select("schema", "name", "dtype").rows())
print(result.to_polars(annotations=True).select("value", "unit", "flag").rows())

Output:

time,time_zone,value,unit
2020-01-10T00:00:00.000000,unknown,34.39,m3/s
2020-01-11T00:00:00.000000,unknown,32.14,m3/s
2
[('jp_mlit.observations', 'flag', 'String')]
[(34.39, 'm3/s', None), (32.14, 'm3/s', None)]

The two rows give discharge in m³/s for January 10 and 11. Both days have a measured value and no cell flag (flag=null). Unmeasured days elsewhere in the annual file remain excluded from result.data and outside the clipped 2020-01-10 to 2020-01-11 annotation table. RivRetrieve returns only the requested dates.

The time zone is unknown, so these timestamps should not be read as UTC or Japan Standard Time. See Time for how the source labels are represented, and Usage for general selection and result inspection.

docs.title: Who measures, and who publishes
docs.text:
MLIT publishes observations through the Water Information System, 水文水質データベース. Its homepage describes stations under the jurisdiction of its Water and Disaster Management Bureau:

このデータベースは水文水質にかかわる国土交通省水管理・国土保全局が所管する観測所における観測データを公開することを目的としています。

In English, unofficially: this database aims to publish observation data from stations under the jurisdiction of MLIT's Water and Disaster Management Bureau. This quotation is retained from the original provider documentation; the homepage content could not be independently rechecked on 2026-09-21.

Station pages identify the responsible local office. For example, the retained page for 茂志利 (Moshiri), station 301011281104010, names MLIT's Asahikawa Development and Construction Department as manager. Administration and publication do not establish who physically made every measurement. This provider does not claim to cover all Japanese hydrometry.

RivRetrieve reads the database's observation pages and their linked download files.

docs.title: What you can retrieve
docs.text:
Quantity filter Source field / variant Frequency Statistic Source unit Returned unit stage KIND 2 Hourly Unknown m m stage KIND 3 Daily Unknown m m discharge KIND 6 Hourly Unknown m³/s m³/s discharge KIND 7 Daily Unknown m³/s m³/s

The catalogue lists these four candidates at each station. A station being listed does not guarantee data for every quantity or requested period. The source station inventory does not establish that availability.

RivRetrieve returns source-published values. It does not calculate daily values from hourly observations. The statistic, averaging period, hours covered by a daily value and stage datum have not been established for these records.

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
Returned time values are source clock labels accompanied by time_zone="unknown". Do not interpret them as UTC or assign Japan Standard Time from the station's location. The datetime column itself has no time zone.

Daily dates are represented at midnight. Hourly source labels run from 1 to 24; 24 is represented at midnight on the following date. These representations do not establish an interval's start or end, an averaging period, or a hydrological-day definition. With an unknown time zone, RivRetrieve cannot convert these labels to UTC.

docs.title: Data status
docs.text:
MLIT's notes on use, retained on 2026-08-21, distinguish provisional and definitive values:

暫定値（青字表記）とは、現在の観測データから過去の統計データまでシームレスにお知らせすることを目的として、無人観測所から送られてくるデータをそのままデータベースに登録公表しているものであり、観測機器の故障、通信異常などによる欠測や異常値を含んでいる可能性があります。

なお、正式に検定されたデータは後日確定値（黒字表記）としてデータベースに登録されますのでこちらを利用して下さい。

In English, unofficially: provisional values (shown in blue) are registered and published as received from unmanned stations. They may contain gaps or anomalies from equipment failure or communication problems. Formally verified data are registered later as definitive values (shown in black), and MLIT asks users to use those values.

MLIT marks provisional values and reasons for missing observations in its download files. RivRetrieve preserves those cell-level symbols in observation-grain annotations (jp_mlit.observations, field flag):

  • A measured value with no flag carries measured=True and flag=null.
  • A measured value marked * (provisional) carries measured=True and flag="*".
  • A calendar slot marked $ (missing), # (station closed), or - (unregistered) produces no numeric observation row in result.data and is retained as an unmeasured annotation slot (measured=False, flag="$", "#", or "-").

The hourly files define all four markers; the daily files define only $ and -. Use result.to_polars(annotations=True) or result.to_pandas(annotations=True) to join measured flags onto observation rows, or call rr.annotations(result, schema="jp_mlit.observations") to inspect both measured rows and unmeasured (measured=False) slots within the requested window. See Source annotations for general options.

RivRetrieve makes no quality judgement of its own. A number without a marker does not establish that MLIT has formally verified it. Daily month rows carry only the valid calendar days of each month (for example 28 days in a non-leap February), so non-existent dates never appear as observation or annotation slots. A failed request is reported separately in result.issues. See Usage for interpreting issues and empty results.

docs.title: Automated access and caching
docs.text:
MLIT's notes on use describe the website as intended for ordinary browser viewing:

ツール等による、自動的なデータ収集等はサーバに負荷がかかり、情報提供できなくなる恐れがありますので原則としてご遠慮ください。

In English, unofficially: please refrain in principle from automatic data collection using tools, because it loads the server and may prevent information provision. This quotation comes from the 2026-08-21 recording.

On 2026-09-21, software requests to the homepage, notes on use and terms PDF returned HTTP 403 with “This site prohibits data acquisition using tools, etc.” The observation example above succeeded that day. Technical success does not establish unrestricted permission for automated access.

RivRetrieve retrieves programmatically. Keep requests limited to the stations, quantities and periods needed for the study. Local caching can reduce repeated requests; it does not create an exemption from MLIT's access guidance. MLIT also warns of slower responses during floods and directs real-time users to リアルタイム川の防災情報.

Daily retrieval downloads annual files, and hourly retrieval downloads monthly files, even for a short requested period. Returned rows and observation annotations are clipped to the requested period before return.

Live retrieval defaults to cache="bypass", which neither reads nor writes the observation cache. To reuse a download, select the specific series and use cache="reuse", as below. Run this example in the same Python session as the first.

series_id = rr.series(selection)["series_id"].item()
chosen = rr.pick(selection, series_id=series_id)

cached_result = rr.fetch(
    chosen, start="2020-01-10", end="2020-01-11", cache="reuse"
)

repeated_result = rr.fetch(
    chosen, start="2020-01-10", end="2020-01-11", cache="reuse"
)

print(repeated_result.data.select("value", "unit").rows())
print(repeated_result.to_polars(annotations=True).select("value", "flag").rows())

Output:

[(34.39, 'm3/s'), (32.14, 'm3/s')]
[(34.39, None), (32.14, None)]

With an initially empty cache, the first reuse call retrieves and stores this series, period, and its cell annotations. The repeated covered request reads locally and preserves the attached annotations. The earlier bypass call did not populate the cache. Selecting the specific series tells RivRetrieve exactly which record to reuse. Repeating the broader selection alone can require another source request because RivRetrieve has not established whether other matching series exist.

The saved acquisition history includes both the HTML page and its linked DAT download, with their original request details and retrieval times. A local read keeps this history even when receipts are disabled. When receipts are enabled, direct retrieval can return both publisher responses; reuse returns a generated excerpt of the saved observations, not copies of those responses.

If the complete request is not covered, reuse retrieves the full requested scope again, rather than downloading only missing dates. Saved values can differ from later source corrections. Use cache="refresh" to request a current answer. Set RIVRETRIEVE_CACHE_DIR to choose a local cache location; see Usage.

Older MLIT caches can lack the HTML request in their saved acquisition history. RivRetrieve refuses these caches before making a request, including when cache="refresh" is selected. Use rr.clear_cache("jp_mlit") to remove the provider’s saved observations, then retrieve the required series again. This creates new acquisition history and retrieval times; it cannot restore the missing original request.

docs.title: Terms and citation
docs.text:
The retained notes on use state:

水文水質データベースをご利用いただく際、掲載しているデータの利用について、許可等は必要ありません。「公共データ利用規約（第1.0版）」に従い、データをご利用ください。

In English, unofficially: no permission is needed to use the published data; use them according to the Public Data Terms of Use, version 1.0 (PDL1.0). This reuse statement is separate from the automated-access guidance above.

The terms PDF, retained on 2026-08-21, says numerical data, simple tables and graphs are outside copyright protection, so these rules do not apply to them and they may be used freely. For content subject to the rules, PDL1.0 permits commercial use and is compatible with CC BY 4.0, with qualifications for third-party rights and statutory restrictions.

Cite the database and consultation date using MLIT's example:

出典：国土交通省 水文水質データベース（https://www1.river.go.jp/）（○年○月○日に参照）、PDL1.0（http://www1.river.go.jp/）

Replace ○年○月○日 with the date of consultation. The PDF requests that date because accuracy checks can lead to updates. It asks for processing and the responsible party to be stated separately from the source, and for processed content not to be presented as the original government content. These terms could not be freshly content-checked on 2026-09-21.
